# Public creation reference

`src/creation.bend` defines immutable scenes, instances, cameras, and compiled
ranges. Mesh and material source values come from
[`src/content.bend`](content.md). Constructors create ordinary unchecked values.
`compile(Scene)` is the checked entry point and returns
`Result<Error,Compiled>`. It needs neither Vulkan nor a window.

## Descriptions

- `Content.Vertex`, `Content.Mesh`, and `Content.Basic` follow the
  [mesh and material contract](content.md). RGB is finite but unrestricted in
  magnitude. Tint is finite and bounded to `[0,1]`.
- `Instance{mesh,material,transform}` creates one initial ECS entity.
  Translation and scale must be finite. Quaternion squared length must lie in
  `[0.9999,1.0001]`.
- `Scene{instances}` preserves instance order through compilation and bootstrap.

`compile` first rejects more than 100,000 instances with `TooLarge`. It then
validates instances in source order. Each instance reports `BadMesh` before
`BadMaterial`, then `BadTransform`, carrying the zero-based instance position.
A source mesh over the current 381,300-vertex or 3,000,000-index profile reports
`BadMesh`. A new pair that overflows aggregate packed counts reports `TooLarge`.
A duplicate pair reuses its range before any aggregate growth check. Validation
and packing complete before any GPU allocation.

Compilation materializes only used mesh/material pairs. Bitwise structural
comparison identifies identical source values. First occurrences determine
range order. Repeated pairs share a range while retaining separate ECS entities.
References start at 7 to preserve the existing demonstration's mesh reference.
Applications consume generated references instead of selecting them.

`Compiled{seeds,geometry}` is the single result. Each `Seed{transform,mesh}`
contains the existing `MeshRef`, which identifies baked geometry. It is not an
entity identity. `Geometry{vertices,indices,ranges}` contains tinted vertices,
rebased indices, and `Range{id,first_index,index_count,texture}` values.
The texture is `None` for Basic materials and `Some{SourceImage}` for textured materials.
Positions, UVs, and normals remain unchanged. `resolve(ranges,id)` returns the matching range or `None`.

`Scene.create(seeds)` registers the existing Bendvy application. The first tick
queues and publishes initial entities, then runs the existing movement system.
Bendvy handles identify entities. A second tick moves existing entities without
spawning them again. Reservation refusal retains ownership through the existing
bootstrap error path. There is no new runtime asset service or material column.

Both renderers accept `Geometry`, validate its bounds before allocating, and
preflight every extracted drawing before recording commands. They issue the
range's actual first index and count in extraction order with the existing
camera/model matrix push. Zero-index ranges issue no draw or push commands.
Geometry with no indices owns no vertex or index buffers. Framebuffer clears
and presentation still run.

## Camera

`Camera{target,yaw,pitch,distance,projection}` defines an orbit around `target`.
`Perspective{scale,near,far}` uses the vertical projection scale, equivalent to
`cot(vertical_fov / 2)`. All values must be finite. Distance, scale, and near
must be positive, and far must exceed near.

`camera(value)` returns `Some` for a valid configuration and `None` otherwise.
`view(camera,width,height)` returns a finite matrix or `None`. Invalid cameras,
zero dimensions, and non-finite derived matrices return `None`.
`default_camera()` preserves the old orbit and projection arithmetic. The demo
applies its own tick-one framing separately.

`Input.key` changes orbit values while preserving target and projection. Reset
restores yaw `0.65`, pitch `0.45`, and distance `7.0`, preserving the configured
target and lens. Reset does not restore a caller's custom initial orbit.
Controls retain the existing pitch clamp `[0.1,1.4]` and distance clamp `[4,15]`.

## Startup callbacks

The four slots in `src/modules.bend` have these concrete inputs and outputs:

| Slot | Callback |
| --- | --- |
| `Core<A>` | `List<Seed> -> IO(A)` |
| `Input` | `Unit -> Camera` |
| `Assets` | `Unit -> Scene` |
| `Render` | `V.Entry -> Geometry -> V.Action(Win.Renderer)` |

The existing executable calls Assets once, compiles once, sends its geometry to
Render, and sends the same result's seeds to Core. Core retains responsibility
for its first tick. The example recipe owns the former fixed 100-entity seeds.
Render adapters are engine assembly code and retain Vulkan access. The public
creation example imports no Vulkan module and handles no Vulkan values.

## Scope

Creation supplies startup entities and packed renderer geometry. Both renderers
support [whole-mesh replacement](mesh-replacement.md), including deferred destruction
and preservation on rejected candidates. [Textured materials](textured-materials.md)
use the same geometry and camera APIs. Runtime entity insertion, per-asset deletion,
transparency, and persistent GPU scene storage remain separate work.
Packing uses sequential structural lookup for small startup scenes. No
performance or cross-backend bitwise determinism claim is made.

The [verification record](verification/2026-11-03-public-creation/README.md)
records formal claims, real ECS execution, offscreen rendering, and X11 captures.
# JSON scene files and manifests

`SceneFile.load(path)` reads a flat scene, resolves its manifest, validates every
declared OBJ and PNG source, and returns `Creation.Scene`. Errors are
`Asset.Error` values. Loading creates no ECS or Vulkan resources. The caller can
cache the result through `Asset.load` and compile it through `Creation.compile`.

```python
import ./src/scene-file.bend as SceneFile

def load(path:String) -> IO(Result<&2,&2,Asset.Error,Creation.Scene>)
def load_manifest(path:String) -> IO(Result<&2,&2,Asset.Error,List<&2,SceneFile.Source>>)
```

`load_manifest` returns ordered `ModelSource{id,value}` and
`ImageSource{id,value}` entries after all declared files load successfully.
`decode_manifest(bytes,path)` and `decode_scene(bytes,path)` validate JSON into
`Manifest` and `Description` without file access. Their `path` argument supplies
diagnostic context. `load` additionally resolves references and checks that the
result compiles through the existing Creation rules. No partial scene is
returned on failure.

## Version 1 schema

Every listed field is required. Unknown fields and wrong types are errors at
all object levels. Object field order is irrelevant. Array order is preserved.
Version is the exact JSON integer token `1`.

A manifest has this shape.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "assets": [
    {"id": "sign", "kind": "obj", "path": "sign.obj"},
    {"id": "image", "kind": "png", "path": "image.png"}
  ]
}
```

A scene has this shape.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "manifest": "manifest.json",
  "instances": [
    {
      "model": "sign",
      "transform": {
        "position": [0, 0, 0],
        "rotation": [0, 0, 0, 1],
        "scale": [1, 1, 1]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

IDs contain 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores. They are
case-sensitive and unique across both asset kinds. Each scene model reference
must name an OBJ entry. A PNG entry cannot be used as a model. Every declared
asset loads, including unused entries. Missing files and malformed OBJ, MTL,
or PNG contents fail the load.

The manifest path is relative to the scene file. Each asset path is relative
to the manifest file. Paths contain printable ASCII slash-separated components.
Empty components, `.` and `..`, backslashes, colons, spaces, and control bytes
are rejected. These are lexical path rules. They do not confine symlink targets
or provide a filesystem sandbox. Root paths must be nonempty, contain no NUL,
and fit within 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Joined paths have the same limit.

A model's parts expand in order at each placement. Meshes, materials, winding,
and transforms are preserved. Existing Creation compilation shares identical
mesh/material pairs. Images remain source assets. This schema adds no texture
binding, cameras, parent hierarchy, animation, or new model format.

## Parser and limits

Both document kinds use only `bend-kit-json@0.7.0.0`, content hash
`0x37aacddc1dcb57464b8b5ac6c397bd64`, through
`parse.strict.unique.bytes`. Its byte storage is
`bend-kit-bytes@0.3.3.0`, hash `0x632652e3c1c0183f12728faf3870bb68`.
Strict UTF-8, complete JSON consumption, valid escapes, and unique decoded
object keys are required. Duplicate keys are rejected even when written with
different escape spellings. Neither first nor last duplicate wins.

The parser retains numeric tokens exactly. Version validation uses that text.
Transform values use `F32.read` only after JSON syntax validation and a numeric
token length check. The resulting F32 must be finite and within
`[-1000000,1000000]`. Decimal values round to F32, including underflow to signed
zero. Position and scale contain exactly three numbers. Rotation contains
exactly four numbers in x/y/z/w order. Its squared norm must be within
`[0.9999,1.0001]`. Loading does not normalize it. Zero and negative scale remain
valid under the existing Creation contract.

| Boundary | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Each scene or manifest | 65536 encoded bytes |
| Nested arrays and objects | 8, checked before parsing contents |
| Decoded string field | 255 UTF-8 bytes |
| Transform numeric token | 64 ASCII bytes |
| Manifest entries | 64 |
| Scene placements | 256 |
| Expanded model parts | 4096 |
| Aggregate loaded source geometry | 381300 vertices and 3000000 indices |
| Aggregate loaded image pixels | 16777216 |
| Each OBJ, MTL, or PNG | Existing importer limits apply |

The file boundary checks size before reading, requests at most size plus one
byte, and rejects a read whose count differs from the measured size. It closes
the file on success and failure. This detects incomplete reads and size changes.
It does not make same-size concurrent edits transactional. Decoding supplied
bytes checks the encoded limit and rejects words above 255 before packing.
Aggregate source limits are checked after each asset decodes. One candidate
asset can temporarily exceed the aggregate budget before rejection.

Adapter errors use `2147484160 + code`. Codes 1 through 6 identify invalid JSON,
a size limit, schema mismatch, numeric or Creation rejection, a reference or
path error, and an incomplete read. File and importer errors retain their own
codes. JSON diagnostics include the document path and the affected schema
location when available. The chosen parser returns a single failure result for
syntax, duplicate keys, and excessive depth, so these share code 1.

## Verification

Run `bend tools/verify-workflow.bend -o build/verify-workflow`, inspect
`./build/verify-workflow --plan json`, then run
`./build/verify-workflow json +RTS --threads 1 --gpu off`.
The JSON profile includes the existing asset checks and root law checks.
`tools/verify-json.bend` retains parser qualification, real file rejection
checks, cache behavior, six production mutations, a restored runtime baseline,
and real ECS/offscreen comparison against an independently authored scene.

The [retained scene](verification/2026-11-04-json-scene/corpus/scene.json) runs
through `examples/json-scene.bend`. Its expected compilation has six instances,
18 vertices, 18 indices, and three shared ranges. The
[verification record](verification/2026-11-04-json-scene/README.md) states the
source receipt and evidence limits.
# Textured materials and directional lighting

Entangle renders `Content.Textured{tint,image}` through the existing offscreen
and X11 Vulkan paths. `image` is a retained `Content.SourceImage`, including an
image loaded through `Asset` and the PNG adapter. Source-cache release does not
destroy GPU resources or invalidate retained scene values.

## Public data and rendering

`Vertex{position,color,uv,normal}` carries eleven finite floats. `UV{u,v}` uses a
top-left origin. Normals are local vectors with squared length in `(1e-12,1e12]`.
Procedural producers supply their surface normals. Existing Basic producers and
the position-only OBJ adapter use default UV `(0,0)` and normal `(0,0,1)`.
OBJ texture coordinates, normal import, and material texture-file resolution
remain outside that adapter's supported profile.

The upload format has a 44-byte stride. Position, color, UV, and normal start at
bytes 0, 12, 24, and 32. The 16 MiB vertex transport bound admits 381,300 vertices.
`render-format.bend` owns the serialized words and image-byte conversion.
The vertex-stride and RGBA-order laws constrain those production definitions.

`Basic` remains unlit. `Textured` uses the same baked RGB tint, samples RGB,
and applies an ambient term plus directional Lambert diffuse lighting.
Both outputs are opaque. Vertex color is flat, while UVs and world normals use
perspective-correct interpolation. Source numerical `0xRRGGBBAA` pixels become
RGBA bytes explicitly. Sampling uses `R8G8B8A8_UNORM`, one mip level, nearest
filtering, and clamp-to-edge addressing. There is no gamma conversion, blending,
normal mapping, or shadow map.

Textures have positive dimensions no larger than 4096 on either axis and at
most 4,194,304 pixels. The pixel list must match the dimensions exactly.
The device's image-format limits are checked before allocation. Each used
textured mesh/material pair owns its descriptor and texture resources. Identical
pairs share their compiled range. Different materials can upload the same source
image separately.

`Lighting.Directional{toward,color,ambient,intensity}` points from the surface
toward the light. Its color, ambient, and intensity channels lie in `[0,1]`.
The default direction is `(0.4,0.7,1)`, with white light, ambient `0.2`, and
intensity `0.8`. Normal transforms apply inverse scale followed by quaternion
rotation. Textured draws reject scale magnitudes outside `[1e-6,1e6]`.
Interpolated zero normals receive ambient light without a normalization singularity.

Offscreen configuration is `Render.Config{width,height,camera,light}`.
`Render.default_light()` returns the default light. `Render.set_light` and
`Window.set_light` return the renderer beside a Boolean acceptance result.
Invalid updates preserve the previous light. `Render.set_camera` accepts the
existing `Creation.Camera`, computes the view for the target extent, and also
preserves the previous configuration on rejection. Window frames continue to use
`Creation.view(camera,width,height)`. Camera or light changes do not upload meshes
or textures again.

The native shaders use at most 128 push-constant bytes. Shader source and generated
SPIR-V live under `src/shaders`. Rebuild with `bend tools/build-scene-shaders.bend`.
For a read-only regeneration check, compile that tool and run its binary with
`--check`. The generator uses `glslc` targeting Vulkan 1.0 and runs `spirv-val`.
No Vulkan dependency revision or backend-specific core algorithm changes.

## Ownership and replacement

# Entangle verification map

Read this index before choosing checks. Each file maps user actions to existing Bend drivers and observable results. The map describes coverage to run, not a claim that every path passed in the latest session.

## Baseline preconditions

- Run from the repository root with the toolchain and dependency revisions in `toolchain.bend`.
- Use the skill's fresh runtime and owned display for native window checks. Drivers find only their own child window.
- Run the doctor before input. Preserve evidence outside disposable runtime state.
- Run gates that write fixed repository `build` paths sequentially. Do not drive or terminate another session's app.
- Read `AGENTS.md`. Use formal laws, real runtime checks, and live input/replay evidence. Add no unit tests or mocks.

## Driving conventions

The executable `tools/verify-window-session.sh` launcher drives mesh movement. For additional camera-window scenarios, follow that feature recipe with its own owned display and runtime. CPU and offscreen recipes are independent shell invocations. They create their own evidence directory and exit after the real process returns.

For an optional window block, copy `tools/verify-window-session.sh` into the ignored `build/verification` directory, insert the block before its `run window ...` command, and run that copy from the repository root. Keep the copied script with the evidence. Do not edit the shared launcher or run the block after its display has been cleaned up.

Use the exact key symbols and native driver modes in the feature files. Do not infer desktop coverage from a headless run. Do not reuse archived captures as evidence for a new build.

## Proof and skip reporting

Record the feature ID, entry point, command, output, exit status, and resulting state. For UI changes, retain captures, native action/state traces where available, and zero-object shutdown logs. For file output, inspect the resulting file. Report build failures and missing display, validation layer, or device prerequisites explicitly.

A mesh pass covers the mesh entry of camera controls. It does not establish the cube entry. A creation CLI pass does not establish rendered colors or depth. If a change affects multiple entries, run all affected entries or list those skipped.

## Features

Use the [verification profiles](../../../../docs/development.md#run-verification) to select required checks. Profile success is scoped to its listed scenarios.

- [Formal laws](formal-laws.md): production Bend definitions, the universal upload-range theorem, mutation controls, and synchronization records.
- [S41 math qualification](../../../../docs/verification/2026-11-05-jonmath/README.md): explicit candidate adapters, numerical contracts, sensitivity controls, and exact retained scene comparisons through the `math` profile.
- [Source assets](../../../../docs/assets.md#verification-and-limits): typed cache handles, real file loading, cached failures, release/retry, exact retained mesh and material sources, source-only dependency closure, and scene execution after source release.
- [PNG source images](images.md): pinned decoder, retained real images, complete-pixel comparison, file/cache/retry behavior and production mutation controls.
- [Static OBJ sources](models.md): pinned parser, exact mesh/material/label conversion, file/cache/retry, source-only closure, real ECS/offscreen geometry, and owned X11 culling evidence.
- [JSON scene files and manifests](json-scene.md): one pinned parser, strict schema and reference validation, bounded loading, cache/retry, source preservation, and real ECS/offscreen evidence.
- [Checked host uploads](upload-boundary.md): enforced source policy, exact production payload lengths, real Vulkan writes and readback, rejection, and cleanup.
- [Mesh replacement](mesh-replacement.md): both renderer APIs, changed pixels and ranges, rejected-candidate preservation, recorded commands, multiple submissions, uniform and sampled-image descriptor retention, memory aliases, atomic retirement rejection, collection, and cleanup.
- [Native resource failures](resource-failures.md): recording/submission/reset rejection, real allocation failure under a process limit, partial preparation rollback, cleanup diagnostics, terminal teardown, and bounded proofs of production handlers for rare driver errors.
- [Mesh movement](mesh-movement.md): six movement keys, held/repeated/opposing input, release, Space reset, and focus loss.
- [Camera and window controls](camera-window.md): both interactive apps, camera reset, resize, hide/restore, Escape, and Close.
- [Public scene creation](scene-creation.md): scene descriptions, compilation, separate instances, shared geometry, and validation.
- [Headless simulation](headless-simulation.md): eight production ticks, zero-step preservation, split batches, and observations.
- [Offscreen rendering](offscreen-rendering.md): image output, exact coverage/depth, retained draws, and resource cleanup.
- [Textured materials](../../../../docs/textured-materials.md): vertex attributes, PNG cache release, sampling and lighting, camera updates, texture replacement and retention, shader controls, and the textured X11 example.

Application module registration is a developer API described in `docs/modules-registration.md`. This seed map does not claim exhaustive API coverage. Extend it when a task changes an unmapped user path.

  Factory{nextNamespace: U32}
# Detached registration id/name/ordered access metadata. It is not the registered
# runner, its affine Local/capture owner or a capability derived from a string.
type RegistrationMeta is Data:
  RegistrationMeta{id: U32, name: String, access: List<&2,String>}
# Explicit low-level refusal reasons for entity, capacity, namespace or system-id
# admission. Callers must inspect their operation result rather than infer success.
type WorldError is Data:
  ReservationUnauthorized{}
  MissingEntity{}
  CapacityExceeded{}
  NamespaceExhausted{}
  SystemIdExhausted{}
# Affine engine storage/resource owner with allocator and administrative state.
# Raw field construction/destructuring is trusted framework provisioning, not the
# opaque gameplay interface. Schema branding alone does not validate forged fields.
type World<Schema: Data,Store: Type,Resource: Type,Event: Data> is Type:
  World{namespace: U32,allocator: A.Allocator,store: Store,resource: Resource,events: List<&2,Event>,pending:List<Deferred.Command<World<Schema,Store,Resource,Event>>>,registrations: List<&2,RegistrationMeta>,nextSystemId: U32,clock: Clock.State,lifecycle:Notice.Journal<Schema>}
# Raw creation returns the advanced Factory and World on success; rejection
# returns the actual Factory and incoming resource owner without constructing C.
type Creation<Schema: Data,Store: Type,Resource: Type,Event: Data> is Type:
  Created{factory: Factory,world: World<Schema,Store,Resource,Event>}
  CreateRejected{factory: Factory,resource: Resource}
# Reservation admission result. Reserved provides a full handle but does not
# activate it or populate components; rejection includes the allocator refusal.
type Reservation<Schema: Data> is Data:
  Reserved{handle: Handle<Schema>}
  ReservationRejected{error: WorldError}
# Low-level operation decision; returned World is separate. Accepted describes
# that operation, not success of an entire transaction or deferred command queue.
type Status is Data:
  Accepted{}
  Rejected{error: WorldError}
# Metadata-registration result; id allocation is distinct from owning or running
# a system. Exhaustion returns RegistrationRejected without a new registration.
type Registration is Data:
  Registered{id: U32}
  RegistrationRejected{error: WorldError}

# Return administrative time without advancing it. Full epoch is required by readers.
def clock(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Tick.Tick:
  match world:
    case World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,+clock,lifecycle}:(World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},Clock.now(clock))

# Observe this execution's captured tick without advancing administrative time.
def execution_clock(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Tick.Tick:
  match world:
    case World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,+clock,lifecycle}:(World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},Clock.current(clock))

def clock_returned(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,namespace:U32,allocator:A.Allocator,store:C,resource:R,events:List<&2,E>,pending:List<Deferred.Command<World<S,C,R,E>>>,registrations:List<&2,RegistrationMeta>,nextSystemId:U32,changed:Clock.State & Tick.Tick,lifecycle:Notice.Journal<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Tick.Tick:
  (clock,tick)=changed
  (World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},tick)

# Explicit direct/deferred time boundary; this is not system admission.
def advance_clock(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Tick.Tick:
  match world:
    case World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle}:clock_returned(~S,~C,~R,~E,namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,Clock.advance(clock),lifecycle)

# Stamp a canonical write with its captured execution tick or a new direct-edit tick.
def write_clock(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Tick.Tick:
  match world:
    case World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle}:clock_returned(~S,~C,~R,~E,namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,Clock.write(clock),lifecycle)

# Enter only after registration admission; capture one tick for all run writes.
def enter_run(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Tick.Tick:
  match world:
    case World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle}:clock_returned(~S,~C,~R,~E,namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,Clock.enter(clock),lifecycle)

# Exit an executed run on success or failure, preserving administrative progress.
def leave_run(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>) -> World<S,C,R,E>:
  match world:
    case World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle}:World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,Clock.leave(clock),lifecycle}

def ensure_returned(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,namespace:U32,allocator:A.Allocator,store:C,resource:R,events:List<&2,E>,pending:List<Deferred.Command<World<S,C,R,E>>>,registrations:List<&2,RegistrationMeta>,nextSystemId:U32,result:Clock.State & Bool,lifecycle:Notice.Journal<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Bool:
  (clock,owned)=result
  (World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},owned)
# A direct query owns a new scope; a query inside a system reuses that scope.
def ensure_run(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Bool:
  match world:
    case World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle}:ensure_returned(~S,~C,~R,~E,namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,Clock.ensure(clock),lifecycle)
def finish_run(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,owned:Bool,world:World<S,C,R,E>) -> World<S,C,R,E>:
  match world:
    case World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle}:World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,Clock.finish(owned,clock),lifecycle}

# Extract only the slot index for trusted storage adapters. Generation and World
# namespace are omitted; this projection must not replace handle validation.
def handle_index(~S:Data,handle:Handle<S>) -> U32:
  match handle:
    case Handle{_,key}:K.index(key)
# Extract the complete index/generation key, without checking namespace or liveness.
def handle_key(~S:Data,handle:Handle<S>) -> K.Key:
  match handle:
    case Handle{_,key}:key

# Start a raw namespace sequence at one. This pure constructor is not a global
# uniqueness service; ordinary independently created Worlds use world-io.bend.
def factory() -> Factory:
  Factory{1}
def create_checked(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,~empty:Unit -> C,available:Bool,+namespace:U32,resource:R) -> Creation<S,C,R,E>:
  match available:
    case False{}:CreateRejected{Factory{namespace},resource}
    case True{}:Created{Factory{(namespace + 1 : U32)},World{namespace,A.empty(),empty(Unit{}),resource,[],[],[],1,Clock.empty(),Notice.empty(~S,namespace)}}
# Consume the raw Factory and resource owner to construct an empty World, advancing
# the namespace sequence on success. Namespace exhaustion returns both inputs via
# CreateRejected. Trusted empty supplies C; use world-io for application creation.
def create(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,~empty:Unit -> C,factory:Factory,resource:R) -> Creation<S,C,R,E>:
  match factory:
    case Factory{+namespace}:create_checked(~S,~C,~R,~E,~empty,U32.is_lt(namespace,4294967295),namespace,resource)
def reserve_result(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,+namespace:U32,store:C,resource:R,+events:List<&2,E>,pending:List<Deferred.Command<World<S,C,R,E>>>,+registrations:List<&2,RegistrationMeta>,+nextSystemId:U32,+clock:Clock.State,allocator:A.Allocator,reservation:A.Reservation,lifecycle:Notice.Journal<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Reservation<S>:
  match reservation:
    case A.Exhausted{}:(World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},ReservationRejected{CapacityExceeded{}})
    case A.Reserved{key}:(World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},Reserved{Handle{namespace,key}})
def reserve_join(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,+namespace:U32,store:C,resource:R,+events:List<&2,E>,pending:List<Deferred.Command<World<S,C,R,E>>>,+registrations:List<&2,RegistrationMeta>,+nextSystemId:U32,+clock:Clock.State,reserved:A.Allocator & A.Reservation,lifecycle:Notice.Journal<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Reservation<S>:
  (allocator,reservation) = reserved
  reserve_result(~S,~C,~R,~E,namespace,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,allocator,reservation,lifecycle)
# Reserve a full allocator key, returning World in both success and refusal.
# Reservation consumes allocator progress and is not yet visible as a live entity.
def reserve_id(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Reservation<S>:
  match world:
    case World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle}:reserve_join(~S,~C,~R,~E,namespace,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,A.reserve(allocator),lifecycle)
def checked_join(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,namespace:U32,store:C,resource:R,events:List<&2,E>,pending:List<Deferred.Command<World<S,C,R,E>>>,registrations:List<&2,RegistrationMeta>,nextSystemId:U32,clock:Clock.State,checked:A.Allocator & Bool,lifecycle:Notice.Journal<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Bool:
  match checked:
    case (allocator,valid):(World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},valid)
def checked_namespace(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,allowed:Bool,mode:U32,world:World<S,C,R,E>,key:K.Key) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Bool:
  match allowed world:
    case False{} world:(world,False{})
    case True{} World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle}:checked_join(~S,~C,~R,~E,namespace,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,A.checked(allocator,key,mode),lifecycle)
def checked(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,mode:U32,world:World<S,C,R,E>,handle:Handle<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Bool:
  match world handle:
    case World{+namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle} Handle{ns,key}:checked_namespace(~S,~C,~R,~E,U32.is_eq(namespace,ns),mode,World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},key)
# Trusted structural check of namespace and current allocator key metadata, without
# requiring a live entity. Not a gameplay substitute for valid.
def metadata_valid(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>,handle:Handle<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Bool:
  checked(~S,~C,~R,~E,0,world,handle)
# Return World with namespace/full-generation/live validation. Foreign or stale
# handles fail before allocator slot access for an unmatched namespace.
def valid(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>,handle:Handle<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Bool:
  checked(~S,~C,~R,~E,1,world,handle)
# Return World with validation of actual Pending authority for this full handle.
# An arbitrary reserved key does not by itself establish that pending authority.
def pending_valid(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>,handle:Handle<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Bool:
  checked(~S,~C,~R,~E,2,world,handle)
def phase_checked(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,phase:A.Phase,key:K.Key,checked:World<S,C,R,E> & Bool) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Status:
  match checked:
    case (world,False{}):(world,Rejected{MissingEntity{}})
    case (World{namespace,allocator,store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},True{}):(World{namespace,A.write_phase(allocator,key,phase),store,resource,events,pending,registrations,nextSystemId,clock,lifecycle},Accepted{})
# Trusted lifecycle phase change after metadata validation; returns World and
# Status. This does not construct components or execute a pending populate closure.
def activate(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>,+handle:Handle<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Status:
  phase_checked(~S,~C,~R,~E,A.Live{},handle_key(~S,handle),metadata_valid(~S,~C,~R,~E,world,handle))
# Opaque storage is retained; this operation cannot make its slot reusable.
# Mark a metadata-valid entity DeadRetained, returning Status and World. Payloads
# remain in storage; schema cleanup must precede slot release/reuse.
def deactivate(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,world:World<S,C,R,E>,+handle:Handle<S>) -> World<S,C,R,E> & Status:
  phase_checked(~S,~C,~R,~E,A.DeadRetained{},handle_key(~S,handle),metadata_valid(~S,~C,~R,~E,world,handle))
def discard_status(~S:Data,~C:Type,~R:Type,~E:Data,observed:World<S,C,R,E> & Status) -> World<S,C,R,E>:
  match observed:
    case (world,_):world

type Viewed<-P:Type,-V:Data> is Type:
  Viewed{owner:P,view:V}
def read(~P:Type,~V:Data,value:Viewed<P,V>) -> Viewed<P,V> & V:
  match value:
    case Viewed{owner,+view}:(Viewed{owner,view},view)
def initialized(-P:Type,-V:Data,result:P & V) -> Viewed<P,V>:
  match result:
    case (owner,view):Viewed{owner,view}

type Layout is Type:
  EmptyLayout{}
  LayoutLeaf{P:Type,V:Data,refresh:P -> P & V,key:String,access:Policy.Policy}
  ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{P:Type,V:Data,refresh:P -> P & V,key:String,persistence:Fragment.PersistenceKind,access:Policy.Policy}
  LayoutPair{left:Layout,right:Layout}
type Route is Data:
  AtLeaf{}
  InLeft{rest:Route}
  InRight{rest:Route}
type ColumnSlot<-S:Data,-P:Type,-key:String,-origin:Layout> is Type:
  ColumnSlot{column:Column.Column<S,P>}
type ResourceSlot<-S:Data,-P:Type,-key:String,-origin:Layout> is Type:
  ResourceSlot{owner:P,stamp:Lifecycle.Stamp}
def unknown_stamp() -> Lifecycle.Stamp:Lifecycle.Stamp{None{},None{}}
def origin(layout:Layout,route:Route) -> Layout:
  match layout route:
    case LayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,accessPolicy} AtLeaf{}:LayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,accessPolicy}
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,kind,accessPolicy} AtLeaf{}:ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,kind,accessPolicy}
    case LayoutPair{left,_} InLeft{rest}:origin(left,rest)
    case LayoutPair{_,right} InRight{rest}:origin(right,rest)
    case _ _:EmptyLayout{}
# Policy is part of the full canonical origin, independently of persistence.
def policy(layout:Layout,route:Route) -> Policy.Policy:
  match layout route:
    case LayoutLeaf{_,_,_,_,access} AtLeaf{}:access
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{_,_,_,_,_,access} AtLeaf{}:access
    case LayoutPair{left,_} InLeft{rest}:policy(left,rest)
    case LayoutPair{_,right} InRight{rest}:policy(right,rest)
    case _ _:Policy.Ordinary{}
def columns(~S:Data,layout:Layout) -> Type:
  match layout:
    case EmptyLayout{}:Unit
    case LayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,accessPolicy}:ColumnSlot<S,Viewed<P,V>,key,LayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,accessPolicy}>
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,kind,accessPolicy}:ColumnSlot<S,Viewed<P,V>,key,ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,kind,accessPolicy}>
    case LayoutPair{left,right}:Product.Owner<columns(~S,left),columns(~S,right)>
def resources_generic(-S:Data,layout:Layout) -> Type:
  match layout:
    case EmptyLayout{}:Unit
    case LayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,accessPolicy}:ResourceSlot<S,Viewed<P,V>,key,LayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,accessPolicy}>
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,kind,accessPolicy}:ResourceSlot<S,Viewed<P,V>,key,ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,key,kind,accessPolicy}>
    case LayoutPair{left,right}:Product.Owner<resources_generic(S,left),resources_generic(S,right)>
def resources(~S:Data,layout:Layout) -> Type:
  resources_generic(S,layout)

def payload(layout:Layout,route:Route) -> Type:
  match layout route:
    case LayoutLeaf{P,V,_,_,_} AtLeaf{}:P
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{P,V,_,_,_,_} AtLeaf{}:P
    case LayoutPair{left,_} InLeft{rest}:payload(left,rest)
    case LayoutPair{_,right} InRight{rest}:payload(right,rest)
    case _ _:Unit
def view(layout:Layout,route:Route) -> Data:
  match layout route:
    case LayoutLeaf{_,V,_,_,_} AtLeaf{}:V
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{_,V,_,_,_,_} AtLeaf{}:V
    case LayoutPair{left,_} InLeft{rest}:view(left,rest)
    case LayoutPair{_,right} InRight{rest}:view(right,rest)

def stored(layout:Layout,route:Route) -> Type:Viewed<payload(layout,route),view(layout,route)>
def initialize(layout:Layout,route:Route,owner:payload(layout,route)) -> stored(layout,route):
  match layout route owner:
    case LayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,_,_} AtLeaf{} owner:initialized(P,V,refresh(owner))
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{P,V,refresh,_,_,_} AtLeaf{} owner:initialized(P,V,refresh(owner))
    case LayoutPair{left,_} InLeft{rest} owner:initialize(left,rest,owner)
    case LayoutPair{_,right} InRight{rest} owner:initialize(right,rest,owner)
    case EmptyLayout{} _ owner:Viewed{owner,Unit{}}
    case LayoutLeaf{_,_,_,_,_} InLeft{_} owner:Viewed{owner,Unit{}}
    case LayoutLeaf{_,_,_,_,_} InRight{_} owner:Viewed{owner,Unit{}}
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{_,_,_,_,_,_} InLeft{_} owner:Viewed{owner,Unit{}}
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{_,_,_,_,_,_} InRight{_} owner:Viewed{owner,Unit{}}
    case LayoutPair{_,_} AtLeaf{} owner:Viewed{owner,Unit{}}
def rewritten(-P:Type,-Stored:Type,-Out:Type,initialize:P -> Stored,result:P & Out) -> Stored & Out:
  match result:
    case (owner,out):(initialize(owner),out)
def rewrite_view(-P:Type,-V:Data,-Out:Type,initialize:P -> Viewed<P,V>,transform:P -> P & Out,value:Viewed<P,V>) -> Viewed<P,V> & Out:
  match value:
    case Viewed{owner,_}:rewritten(P,Viewed<P,V>,Out,initialize,transform(owner))
def rewrite(~layout:Layout,~route:Route,-Out:Type,transform:payload(layout,route) -> payload(layout,route) & Out,value:stored(layout,route)) -> stored(layout,route) & Out:
  rewrite_view(payload(layout,route),view(layout,route),Out,initialize(layout,route),transform,value)
def key(layout:Layout,route:Route) -> String:

    case LayoutLeaf{_,V,_,key,_} AtLeaf{}:key
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{_,V,_,key,_,_} AtLeaf{}:key
    case LayoutPair{left,_} InLeft{rest}:key(left,rest)
    case LayoutPair{_,right} InRight{rest}:key(right,rest)

def valid(layout:Layout,route:Route) -> Bool:
  match layout route:
    case LayoutLeaf{_,V,_,_,_} AtLeaf{}:True{}
    case ClassifiedLayoutLeaf{_,V,_,_,_,_} AtLeaf{}:True{}
    case LayoutPair{left,_} InLeft{rest}:valid(left,rest)
    case LayoutPair{_,right} InRight{rest}:valid(right,rest)

import Base
import ./upload-boundary/scan.bend as S
import ./verify-upload-mutations.bend as Files
import ../toolchain.bend as Pin

type Step is Data:
  Step{name:String,kind:String,program:String,args:List<&2,String>}

def native(+name:String,kind:String,path:String,args:List<&2,String>) -> List<&2,Step>:
  +binary:String = Bool.pick(String,String.eq(name,"boundary"),"build/verify-upload-boundary","build/workflow-" ++ name)
  [Step{name ++ "-build","build","bend",[path,"-o",binary]},
   Step{name,kind,"./" ++ binary,List.append(&2,String,args,["+RTS","--threads","1","--gpu","off"])}]

def known(name:String) -> Bool:
  S.has(["toolchain","proofs","assets","images","json","math","textures","upload","native-failures","native","window","textured-window","all"],name)

def valid(names:List<&2,String>) -> Bool:
  match names:
    case []:True{}
    case +name <> rest:known(name) && valid(rest)

def selected(+names:List<&2,String>,+name:String) -> Bool:
  S.has(names,name) || S.has(names,"all")

def add(ok:Bool,steps:List<&2,Step>) -> List<&2,Step>:
  Bool.pick(List<&2,Step>,ok,steps,[])

def plan(+names:List<&2,String>) -> List<&2,Step>:
  +baseline:Bool = selected(names,"native")
  +proofs:Bool = selected(names,"proofs")
  +assets:Bool = selected(names,"assets") || selected(names,"images") || selected(names,"json")
  +upload:Bool = selected(names,"upload") || baseline
  +failures:Bool = selected(names,"native-failures") || selected(names,"textures") || baseline
  +laws:Bool = proofs || assets || upload || failures || selected(names,"math")
  List.concat(&2,Step,[
    [Step{"toolchain","precondition","bend",["tools/verify-toolchain.bend"]}],
    add(laws || selected(names,"window") || selected(names,"textured-window"),native("boundary","source-policy","tools/verify-upload-boundary.bend",[])),
    add(laws && Bool.not(baseline),[Step{"frontend","frontend","bend",["PROOF.bend"]}]),
    add(assets && Bool.not(baseline),native("assets","runtime","tools/verify-assets.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"images") && Bool.not(baseline),native("images","runtime-and-sensitivity","tools/verify-images.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"json") && Bool.not(baseline),native("json","runtime-and-sensitivity","tools/verify-json.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"math"),native("math","qualification-and-retained-scenes","tools/verify-math.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"textures") && Bool.not(baseline),native("textures","runtime-and-sensitivity","tools/verify-textures.bend",[])),
    add(upload && Bool.not(baseline),native("upload-runtime","runtime","tools/verify-upload-runtime.bend",[])),
    add(upload && Bool.not(baseline),native("upload-native-limit","runtime","tools/verify-upload-native-limit.bend",[])),
    add(failures && Bool.not(baseline),native("resource-failures","runtime","tools/verify-resource-failures.bend",[])),
    add(baseline,native("native","native-baseline","tools/verify.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"window") && Bool.not(selected(names,"textured-window")),[Step{"window","mesh-window-and-replay","bash",["tools/verify-window-session.sh"]}]),
    add(selected(names,"textured-window"),[Step{"textured-window","all-renderer-windows-and-replay","bash",["tools/verify-window-session.sh","extended"]}]),
    add(proofs || upload,[Step{"upload-kernel","kernel","bend",["proofs/upload-range/PROOF.bend","--verdict"]}]),
    add(laws,native("law-mutations","sensitivity","tools/verify-law-mutations.bend",[])),
    add(upload,native("upload-mutations","sensitivity","tools/verify-upload-mutations.bend",[])),
    add(failures,native("native-failures","bounded-proof-and-sensitivity","tools/verify-native-failures.bend",["--mutations"]))])

def inputs() -> List<&2,String>:
  ["src","tools","examples","assets","proofs","deps","docs",".agents","LAWS.bend","PROOF.bend","toolchain.bend",".gitmodules","AGENTS.md","README.md"]

def linear(values:List<&2,String>) -> List<String>:
  match values:
    case []:[]
    case head <> rest:head <> linear(rest)

def reusable(values:List<String>) -> List<&2,String>:
  match values:
    case []:[]
    case head <> rest:head <> reusable(rest)

def raw(cwd:String,program:String,args:List<&2,String>,input:String) -> IO(Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)>):
  Process.run("env",linear(List.append(&2,String,["-C",cwd,program],args)),input,16777216,3600000)

def output(value:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)>) -> IO(String):
  do IO<String>:
    result:U32 & (String & String) <- IO.try(U32 & (String & String),IO.pure(Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)>,value))
    S.finished("Verification setup",result)

def command(cwd:String,program:String,args:List<&2,String>) -> IO(String):
  do IO<String>:
    result:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)> <- raw(cwd,program,args,"")
    output(result)

def fingerprint(+cwd:String) -> IO(String):
  do IO<String>:
    hashes:String <- command(cwd,"find",List.append(&2,String,inputs(),["-name",".git","-prune","-o","-type","f","-exec","sha256sum","--","{}","+"]))
    sorted:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)> <- raw(cwd,"sort",[],hashes)
    output(sorted)

def lines(values:List<&2,String>) -> String:
  match values:
    case []:""
    case head <> rest:head ++ "\n" ++ lines(rest)

def manifest(steps:List<&2,Step>) -> String:
  match steps:
    case []:""
    case Step{+name,kind,_,_} <> rest:
      name ++ "\t" ++ kind ++ "\t" ++ name ++ ".argv\t" ++ name ++ ".stdout\t" ++ name ++ ".stderr\t" ++ name ++ ".status\n" ++ manifest(rest)

def preview(steps:List<&2,Step>) -> IO(Unit):
  match steps:
    case []:IO.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case Step{name,kind,program,args} <> rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        IO.print(name ++ " [" ++ kind ++ "]")
        IO.write(lines(program <> args))
        preview(rest)

def prepare(+dest:String,steps:List<&2,Step>) -> IO(Unit):
  match steps:
    case []:IO.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case Step{+name,_,program,args} <> rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".argv",lines(program <> args))
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".status","not_run\n")
        prepare(dest,rest)

def recorded(+dest:String,+name:String,result:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)>) -> IO(Bool):
  match result:
    case Fail{(code,message)}:
      do IO<Bool>:
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".stderr",message)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".status","process_error:" ++ U32.show(code) ++ "\n")
        return False{}
    case Done{(+status,(out,err))}:
      do IO<Bool>:
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".stdout",out)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".stderr",err)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".status",U32.show(status) ++ "\n")
        IO.print(name ++ " exit=" ++ U32.show(status))
        return U32.is_zero(status)

def execute(+dest:String,steps:List<&2,Step>) -> IO(Bool):
  match steps:
    case []:IO.pure(Bool,True{})
    case Step{+name,_,program,args} <> rest:
      do IO<Bool>:
        IO.print("Running " ++ name)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".status","running\n")
        result:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)> <- raw(dest ++ "/source",program,args,"")
        ok:Bool <- recorded(dest,name,result)
        Bool.pick(IO(Bool),ok,execute(dest,rest),IO.pure(Bool,False{}))

def metadata(+root:String,+dest:String,+name:String,program:String,args:List<&2,String>) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    text:String <- command(root,program,args)
    Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name,text)

def repository(+root:String,+dest:String,+path:String) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    +copy:String = dest ++ "/source/" ++ path
    +temporary:String = dest ++ "/repository-metadata"
    _:String <- command(root,"git",["clone","--local","--no-hardlinks","--no-checkout","--",root ++ "/" ++ path,temporary])
    _:String <- command(root,"rm",["-rf","--",copy ++ "/.git"])
    _:String <- command(root,"mv",["--",temporary ++ "/.git",copy ++ "/.git"])
    _:String <- command(root,"rmdir",["--",temporary])
    _:String <- command(copy,"git",["read-tree","HEAD"])
    return Unit{}

def repositories(+root:String,+dest:String,dependencies:List<(String & String)>) -> IO(Unit):
  match dependencies:
    case []:IO.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case (path,_) <> rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        repository(root,dest,path)
        repositories(root,dest,rest)

def run(+names:List<&2,String>) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    cwd:String <- S.run("pwd",[])
    +root:String = String.trim(cwd)
    _:String <- command(root,"mkdir",["-p","build/verification"])
    path:String <- command(root,"mktemp",["-d",root ++ "/build/verification/workflow-XXXXXXXX"])
    +dest:String = String.trim(path)
    IO.print("Evidence: " ++ dest)
    Files.save(dest ++ "/run.status","1\n")
    Files.save(dest ++ "/state","preparing\n")
    Files.save(dest ++ "/profiles.txt",lines(names))
    Files.save(dest ++ "/manifest.tsv","stage\tkind\targv\tstdout\tstderr\tstatus\n" ++ manifest(plan(names)))
    prepare(dest,plan(names))
    metadata(root,dest,"started.txt","date",["-u","+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"])
    metadata(root,dest,"revision.txt","git",["rev-parse","HEAD"])

type Step is Data:
  Step{name:String,kind:String,program:String,args:List<&2,String>}

def native(+name:String,kind:String,path:String,args:List<&2,String>) -> List<&2,Step>:
  +binary:String = Bool.pick(String,String.eq(name,"boundary"),"build/verify-upload-boundary","build/workflow-" ++ name)
  [Step{name ++ "-build","build","bend",[path,"-o",binary]},
   Step{name,kind,"./" ++ binary,List.append(&2,String,args,["+RTS","--threads","1","--gpu","off"])}]

def known(name:String) -> Bool:
  S.has(["toolchain","proofs","assets","images","json","math","textures","upload","native-failures","native","window","textured-window","all"],name)

def valid(names:List<&2,String>) -> Bool:
  match names:
    case []:True{}
    case +name <> rest:known(name) && valid(rest)

def selected(+names:List<&2,String>,+name:String) -> Bool:
  S.has(names,name) || S.has(names,"all")

def add(ok:Bool,steps:List<&2,Step>) -> List<&2,Step>:
  Bool.pick(List<&2,Step>,ok,steps,[])

def plan(+names:List<&2,String>) -> List<&2,Step>:
  +baseline:Bool = selected(names,"native")
  +proofs:Bool = selected(names,"proofs")
  +assets:Bool = selected(names,"assets") || selected(names,"images") || selected(names,"json")
  +upload:Bool = selected(names,"upload") || baseline
  +failures:Bool = selected(names,"native-failures") || selected(names,"textures") || baseline
  +laws:Bool = proofs || assets || upload || failures || selected(names,"math")
  List.concat(&2,Step,[
    [Step{"toolchain","precondition","bend",["tools/verify-toolchain.bend"]}],
    add(laws || selected(names,"window") || selected(names,"textured-window"),native("boundary","source-policy","tools/verify-upload-boundary.bend",[])),
    add(laws && Bool.not(baseline),[Step{"frontend","frontend","bend",["PROOF.bend"]}]),
    add(assets && Bool.not(baseline),native("assets","runtime","tools/verify-assets.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"images") && Bool.not(baseline),native("images","runtime-and-sensitivity","tools/verify-images.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"json") && Bool.not(baseline),native("json","runtime-and-sensitivity","tools/verify-json.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"math"),native("math","qualification-and-retained-scenes","tools/verify-math.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"textures") && Bool.not(baseline),native("textures","runtime-and-sensitivity","tools/verify-textures.bend",[])),
    add(upload && Bool.not(baseline),native("upload-runtime","runtime","tools/verify-upload-runtime.bend",[])),
    add(upload && Bool.not(baseline),native("upload-native-limit","runtime","tools/verify-upload-native-limit.bend",[])),
    add(failures && Bool.not(baseline),native("resource-failures","runtime","tools/verify-resource-failures.bend",[])),
    add(baseline,native("native","native-baseline","tools/verify.bend",[])),
    add(selected(names,"window") && Bool.not(selected(names,"textured-window")),[Step{"window","mesh-window-and-replay","bash",["tools/verify-window-session.sh"]}]),
    add(selected(names,"textured-window"),[Step{"textured-window","all-renderer-windows-and-replay","bash",["tools/verify-window-session.sh","extended"]}]),
    add(proofs || upload,[Step{"upload-kernel","kernel","bend",["proofs/upload-range/PROOF.bend","--verdict"]}]),
    add(laws,native("law-mutations","sensitivity","tools/verify-law-mutations.bend",[])),
    add(upload,native("upload-mutations","sensitivity","tools/verify-upload-mutations.bend",[])),
    add(failures,native("native-failures","bounded-proof-and-sensitivity","tools/verify-native-failures.bend",["--mutations"]))])

def linear(values:List<&2,String>) -> List<String>:
  match values:
    case []:[]
    case head <> rest:head <> linear(rest)

def reusable(values:List<String>) -> List<&2,String>:
  match values:
    case []:[]
    case head <> rest:head <> reusable(rest)

def raw(cwd:String,program:String,args:List<&2,String>,input:String) -> IO(Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)>):
  Process.run("env",linear(List.append(&2,String,["-C",cwd,program],args)),input,16777216,3600000)

def output(value:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)>) -> IO(String):
  do IO<String>:
    result:U32 & (String & String) <- IO.try(U32 & (String & String),IO.pure(Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)>,value))
    S.finished("Verification setup",result)

def command(cwd:String,program:String,args:List<&2,String>) -> IO(String):
  do IO<String>:
    result:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)> <- raw(cwd,program,args,"")
    output(result)

def fingerprint(+cwd:String) -> IO(String):
  do IO<String>:
    hashes:String <- command(cwd,"find",List.append(&2,String,inputs(),["-name",".git","-prune","-o","-type","f","-exec","sha256sum","--","{}","+"]))
    sorted:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)> <- raw(cwd,"sort",[],hashes)
    output(sorted)

def lines(values:List<&2,String>) -> String:
  match values:
    case []:""
    case head <> rest:head ++ "\n" ++ lines(rest)

def manifest(steps:List<&2,Step>) -> String:
  match steps:
    case []:""
    case Step{+name,kind,_,_} <> rest:
      name ++ "\t" ++ kind ++ "\t" ++ name ++ ".argv\t" ++ name ++ ".stdout\t" ++ name ++ ".stderr\t" ++ name ++ ".status\n" ++ manifest(rest)

def preview(steps:List<&2,Step>) -> IO(Unit):
  match steps:
    case []:IO.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case Step{name,kind,program,args} <> rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        IO.print(name ++ " [" ++ kind ++ "]")
        IO.write(lines(program <> args))
        preview(rest)

def prepare(+dest:String,steps:List<&2,Step>) -> IO(Unit):
  match steps:
    case []:IO.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case Step{+name,_,program,args} <> rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".argv",lines(program <> args))
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".status","not_run\n")
        prepare(dest,rest)

def recorded(+dest:String,+name:String,result:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)>) -> IO(Bool):
  match result:
    case Fail{(code,message)}:
      do IO<Bool>:
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".stderr",message)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".status","process_error:" ++ U32.show(code) ++ "\n")
        return False{}
    case Done{(+status,(out,err))}:
      do IO<Bool>:
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".stdout",out)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".stderr",err)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".status",U32.show(status) ++ "\n")
        IO.print(name ++ " exit=" ++ U32.show(status))
        return U32.is_zero(status)

def execute(+dest:String,steps:List<&2,Step>) -> IO(Bool):
  match steps:
    case []:IO.pure(Bool,True{})
    case Step{+name,_,program,args} <> rest:
      do IO<Bool>:
        IO.print("Running " ++ name)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name ++ ".status","running\n")
        result:Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,U32 & (String & String)> <- raw(dest ++ "/source",program,args,"")
        ok:Bool <- recorded(dest,name,result)
        Bool.pick(IO(Bool),ok,execute(dest,rest),IO.pure(Bool,False{}))

def metadata(+root:String,+dest:String,+name:String,program:String,args:List<&2,String>) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    text:String <- command(root,program,args)
    Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ name,text)

def repository(+root:String,+dest:String,+path:String) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    +copy:String = dest ++ "/source/" ++ path
    +temporary:String = dest ++ "/repository-metadata"
    _:String <- command(root,"git",["clone","--local","--no-hardlinks","--no-checkout","--",root ++ "/" ++ path,temporary])
    _:String <- command(root,"rm",["-rf","--",copy ++ "/.git"])
    _:String <- command(root,"mv",["--",temporary ++ "/.git",copy ++ "/.git"])
    _:String <- command(root,"rmdir",["--",temporary])
    _:String <- command(copy,"git",["read-tree","HEAD"])
    return Unit{}

def repositories(+root:String,+dest:String,dependencies:List<(String & String)>) -> IO(Unit):
  match dependencies:
    case []:IO.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case (path,_) <> rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        repository(root,dest,path)
        repositories(root,dest,rest)

#version 450
layout(set=0,binding=0) uniform sampler2D albedo;
layout(push_constant) uniform Drawing {
    mat4 mvp;
    vec4 rotation;
    vec4 inverse_scale;
    vec4 light_direction_ambient;
    vec4 light_color_intensity;
} drawing;
layout(location=0) flat in vec3 vertex_color;
layout(location=1) in vec2 texture_uv;
layout(location=2) in vec3 world_normal;
layout(location=0) out vec4 output_color;
void main() {
    float normal_squared = dot(world_normal, world_normal);
    vec3 normal = world_normal * inversesqrt(normal_squared > 0.0 ? normal_squared : 1.0);
    float diffuse = max(dot(normal, normalize(drawing.light_direction_ambient.xyz)), 0.0);
    vec3 light = vec3(drawing.light_direction_ambient.w) + drawing.light_color_intensity.rgb * (drawing.light_color_intensity.w * diffuse);
    output_color = vec4(texture(albedo, texture_uv).rgb * vertex_color * light, 1.0);
}

  Registry.command(~D.World(),~Spawn.Node(),~String,~Unit,~spawn_dispatch(),Author.facts(~D.Schema,~D.components(),

  Registry.ordinary(~D.World(),~Move.Node(),~String,~Unit,~move_dispatch(),Leaf.facts(~D.Schema,~D.components(),

  Retention.publish_pair(~D.World(),~Spawn.Node(),~Move.Node(),~spawn_publish(),~move_publish(),ids,tick,
    world,nodes)

  Retention.collect_pair(~Spawn.Node(),~Move.Node(),~spawn_collect(),~move_collect(),ids,nodes)

def apply(ids:List<&2,U32>,world:D.World(),nodes:Nodes()) -> D.World() & (Nodes() & List<&2,U32>):
  Publication.apply(~D.Schema,~D.Columns(),~D.Resources(),~Unit,~Nodes(),~pending,~publish,~collect,ids,
    world,nodes)

  Reg.empty_dispatch(~D.World(),~String,~Bool)

# Design red flags

Screen every candidate before synthesis. A red flag is a reason to revise or reject the shape.

## Shallow module

A shallow module exposes a large interface while hiding little complexity. Judge depth by the capability and policy hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface backed by substantial behavior.

Do not confuse a deep module with a deep call chain. A deep call chain scatters understanding across layers. A deep module concentrates capability behind one interface.

Look for these signs:

- Callers coordinate several methods to complete one operation.
- Public options expose internal stages or implementation choices.
- Learning the interface does not save the caller from learning the implementation.

## Information leakage

Information leakage makes multiple modules depend on the same internal decision. A representation, policy, or protocol detail appears in more than one place, so changing it requires coordinated edits.

Public re-exports of transport or wire types are leakage. Parse external data into domain types behind the interface. Keep storage schemas, framework objects, and protocol details private.

## Temporal decomposition

Temporal decomposition organizes modules by execution order instead of the knowledge they own. Separate load, validate, transform, and save stages often repeat one representation and its invariants across several boundaries.

Group code around domain knowledge and ownership. Methods that run at different times can still belong to one module when they protect the same decisions.

## Pass-through method

A pass-through method forwards the same arguments to another method with the same shape. It adds a layer without hiding complexity.

Remove it or move responsibility to the module that can complete the operation. Keep a forwarding boundary only when it adds policy, adaptation, or a distinct abstraction.

## Split ownership

More than one module writes the same state or keeps its own copy of it. An agent that edits one writer can't see the others, so their rules diverge.

Give each piece of state one owner. Other modules read it or ask the owner to change it.

## Two ways to do one task

The design supports more than one way to do the same task. An agent copies whichever way it finds first, so every way keeps gaining callers.

Keep one way. Move callers off the others and delete them in the same change.

## Importable internals

A caller can import a module's internals. An agent takes the shortest path that compiles, so it imports them directly and they become part of the interface.

Make internals unreachable from outside the module, so an import from outside fails the build.

## Hand-synced list

Two or more places list the same items, and adding an item means editing every list. An agent that sees one list updates only that one.

Keep one list and derive the others from it. If a list can't be derived, make the build fail when the lists disagree.

# Scene state ownership

The retained `Scene.Application()` owns the authoritative component state through
its Bendvy world. Future simulation chunks must be storage owned by that world,
with exclusive access transferred to a numerical task and returned afterward.
They cannot be an independently writable mirror of ECS components.

This contract completes the E2 ownership decision. Entangle has no simulation
chunk implementation or chunk transfer API yet. R0 must establish which storage
operations the pinned Bend toolchain and Bendvy can support.

## Authoritative state and observations

For each live entity and component, one storage owner determines the next
authoritative value. Several systems can update that storage in schedule order.
A single owner does not mean that only one system may ever write a component.

| Representation | Authority |
| --- | --- |
| `Scene.Application()` and its `D.World()` | Retain component storage, allocator, deferred commands, and schedule state. |
| Registered `GeneralWriter` and its execution scope `H` | Authorize an update of the current component in that world. The operation consumes and returns the scope. |
| `C.Transform`, query row views, and `Observe.Snapshot` | Copyable values. They carry no scope or writer and cannot publish themselves. |
| `Draw.DrawList` | Detached rendering input. It has neither entity handles nor a component writer. |
| Future owned simulation chunks | A partition of authoritative storage while tasks hold it. Ordinary ECS access to that partition must be unavailable until ownership returns. |
| Future halos, neighbor snapshots, and render projections | Derived read inputs with a defined observation phase. They do not authorize component replacement. |

`World`, the retained application state, and the schedule wrapper have kind
`Type`. Bend's affine checker prevents reusing the same owner. Component records
have kind `Data`, so copying a transform remains legal and useful.

Affinity alone does not establish this contract. Two separately allocated affine
arrays can contain independently evolving copies of the same components. A
component handle also identifies an entity without granting access to its storage.

## Current write path

[`scene-schema.bend`](../src/scene-schema.bend) registers ordinary `Transform` and
`MeshRef` columns. Its payload-to-view projections copy values for observation.
They do not transfer component storage to the reader.

[`scene.bend`](../src/scene.bend) retains the world inside `Scene.Application()`.
`Scene.run` consumes that application and returns its successor with a schedule
report. Bootstrap publishes initial components before the movement system runs.

[`scene-motion.bend`](../src/scene-motion.bend) requests a `WriteRows` capability
for transforms on entities with `MeshRef`. `move_rows` uses the selected handle
and discards the row's copied transform. `GeneralWriter.modify` supplies the
current stored transform to `translate`, which calls `Step.step` and returns the
replacement. Each call returns the scope used by the next row.

Calling `Step.step` on a snapshot calculates a detached value. It does not update
the scene. Production movement has no snapshot-to-world writeback operation.
Later systems must also update through the owner instead of installing values
computed from an earlier observation without an explicit conflict policy.

Numerical writes are immediate. A refused query returns the incoming scope.
A refused write stops movement and retains earlier accepted writes. Structural
commands publish at the schedule's apply boundaries. Ownership transfer must not
silently turn these operations into an atomic batch or add rollback. See the
[headless reference](headless-reference.md) and
[schedule visibility contract](schedule-visibility.md).

[`scene-observe.bend`](../src/scene-observe.bend) consumes and reconstructs the
application around a read-only inspector. Snapshots and drawing data may outlive
the observation. Rendering or replaying them cannot restore an older scene.

## Future chunk integration

The selected model keeps ECS as the persistent owner. Chunk layout is an internal
storage choice. A work batch describes computation over that storage and need
not have the same boundaries as a storage chunk.

A future transfer API must represent these conditions in its types and checked
operations before production simulation uses it:

1. The simulation adapter consumes the owner or an exclusive storage capability.
   Partitioning transfers payload ownership. It does not clone canonical fields
   into a second persistent container.
2. Each task receives exclusive access to its assigned partition. Partition
   membership covers the selected entities without overlap. Entity handles retain
   their namespace and generation and do not become unchecked physical indexes.
3. While tasks hold partitions, the remaining coordinator cannot obtain an ECS
   reader or writer for those partitions. A usable world and writable detached
   chunks must never coexist for the same components.
4. Cross-partition reads use a specified read-only representation, such as a
   bounded snapshot from tick start. That representation carries no writeback
   permission. Its phase and copy costs are part of the algorithm's contract.
5. Completion returns each owned partition through the same adapter before
   ordinary ECS access and extraction resume. A refused or cancelled operation
   must account for every partition and define the resulting authoritative state.
6. Structural changes that invalidate partition membership or storage addresses
   wait for ownership to return. Their publication order follows the explicit
   schedule contract. Render extraction observes a completed state boundary.

These are requirements for a future API, not descriptions of a shipped lease or
split operation. The pinned dependency's `chunk-column.Column` is an affine
storage implementation. Its existence does not establish a safe Entangle task
handoff. If exclusive transfer cannot be expressed, simulation remains sequential
through the current ECS writer. Independently allocated chunks may be canonical
storage if the world owns them without retaining writable duplicate columns.

R0 may run a standalone numerical reference from copied initial values. That is
a separate execution for comparison, not a live mirror with a writeback path.
CPU or GPU dispatch changes execution only. The ownership and numerical contract
must remain the same without GPU dispatch.

## Excluded designs and trusted boundary

A permanent ECS store plus a mutable simulation mirror violates this contract,
even if a scheduler runs their writers sequentially or synchronizes them every
frame. The contract also excludes restoring a retained draw list, snapshot, or
neighbor halo as current component state.

Moving persistent authority outside ECS would require a separate design change.
That change must remove writable ECS storage for those fields, expose derived
read projections, and route edits as commands to the simulation owner. A second
store cannot be introduced as an incremental compatibility path.

Trusted provisioning code can construct raw world records and register writers.
The current public Bendvy constructors do not make this repository an opaque
capability sandbox. The contract constrains those callers too. The affine checker
prevents owner reuse, but it does not forbid an engineer from adding a new store.
Future chunk integration therefore needs production-path ownership checks and
must remove any duplicate writer path in the same change.

## Verification and limits

`LAWS.bend` states general claims against the current production adapter:

- `scene_move_view_independent` proves that substituting any optional head-row
  view leaves traversal unchanged for arbitrary remaining rows and scope.
- `scene_move_current_component` proves that traversal passes `Move.translate`
  to the supplied writer for that handle, then continues with the returned scope.
- `scene_move_query_refusal` proves that a refused query returns the incoming
  scope with the query error and does not call the writer.
- `scene_step_adapter` binds that callback to the numerical kernel. Existing
  kernel laws specify its translation, preserved rotation and scale, and output.

`PROOF.bend` checks these claims. They assume the supplied writer's contract and
do not prove every Bendvy storage operation or prevent future duplicate stores.
The native verifier exercises the actual registered writer across eight ticks,
checks every entity's identity and transform, and checks detached render replay.

```sh
bend PROOF.bend
bend tools/verify.bend
```

The [verification record](verification/2026-11-03-state-ownership/README.md)
records the runs and their limits. R0 and R1 still need checks for partition
coverage, unavailable competing writers, ownership return on failure, and
equivalence with the sequential reference. No future chunk implementation is
proved by the current adapter laws.

def record(result:U32 & (String & String),+dest:String,+label:String,+failure:String) -> IO(Unit):

  +log:String = out ++ err
  +negative:Bool = Bool.not(String.eq(failure,""))
  do IO<Unit>:
    Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ label ++ ".log",log)

      U32.is_zero(status) && String.contains(log,"ALL PROOFS CHECK")),

# Design red flags

Screen every candidate before synthesis. A red flag is a reason to revise or reject the shape.

## Shallow module

A shallow module exposes a large interface while hiding little complexity. Judge depth by the capability and policy hidden behind the public surface relative to the size of that surface. Prefer a simple interface backed by substantial behavior.

Do not confuse a deep module with a deep call chain. A deep call chain scatters understanding across layers. A deep module concentrates capability behind one interface.

Look for these signs:

- Callers coordinate several methods to complete one operation.
- Public options expose internal stages or implementation choices.
- Learning the interface does not save the caller from learning the implementation.

## Information leakage

Information leakage makes multiple modules depend on the same internal decision. A representation, policy, or protocol detail appears in more than one place, so changing it requires coordinated edits.

Public re-exports of transport or wire types are leakage. Parse external data into domain types behind the interface. Keep storage schemas, framework objects, and protocol details private.

## Temporal decomposition

Temporal decomposition organizes modules by execution order instead of the knowledge they own. Separate load, validate, transform, and save stages often repeat one representation and its invariants across several boundaries.

Group code around domain knowledge and ownership. Methods that run at different times can still belong to one module when they protect the same decisions.

## Pass-through method

A pass-through method forwards the same arguments to another method with the same shape. It adds a layer without hiding complexity.

Remove it or move responsibility to the module that can complete the operation. Keep a forwarding boundary only when it adds policy, adaptation, or a distinct abstraction.

## Split ownership

More than one module writes the same state or keeps its own copy of it. An agent that edits one writer can't see the others, so their rules diverge.

Give each piece of state one owner. Other modules read it or ask the owner to change it.

## Two ways to do one task

The design supports more than one way to do the same task. An agent copies whichever way it finds first, so every way keeps gaining callers.

Keep one way. Move callers off the others and delete them in the same change.

## Importable internals

A caller can import a module's internals. An agent takes the shortest path that compiles, so it imports them directly and they become part of the interface.

Make internals unreachable from outside the module, so an import from outside fails the build.

## Hand-synced list

Two or more places list the same items, and adding an item means editing every list. An agent that sees one list updates only that one.

Keep one list and derive the others from it. If a list can't be derived, make the build fail when the lists disagree.
