# Scene hierarchy

Implementation task: [Trail 31](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/31).
This contract is recorded before implementation. Verification results are pending.

## Semantics and ownership

Each scene instance has one optional parent, identified by its zero-based source
instance index. Forward references are allowed. Roots have no parent. The graph
must be a forest. Self-parenting, cycles, and missing parents are errors.
Runtime edits use full Bendvy entity handles, including namespace and generation.
An absent parent detaches the object. Reparenting preserves the local transform.
It may change the object's world position. There is no preserve-world operation.
Runtime spawn and despawn remain outside this API.

Local transforms use column vectors and `T * R * S`. A root's GlobalTransform is
its local model matrix. A child's matrix is `parent_global * child_local`.
GlobalTransform retains the complete affine matrix, including shear. It is never
decomposed back into rotation and scale. World bounds enclose the eight transformed
corners of the source mesh AABB. They bound that object's geometry, not its subtree.
Empty geometry has empty bounds. Lighting uses the inverse transpose of the
world linear transform. A singular transform is allowed for unlit geometry;
textured geometry requires a finite, numerically usable inverse.

Creation descriptions are immutable inputs. The ECS owns local transforms,
parent relationships, source bounds, and derived state. A completed tick or
accepted public edit publishes a consistent set of local transforms, globals,
and bounds. GlobalTransform and world bounds have no public setter. Detached
observations and render lists cannot write back to the world. A last-accepted
local value retained with derived state is a rollback checkpoint, not a second
simulation authority.

The baseline recomputes the complete forest sequentially at each publication
boundary. Validation and derivation finish before public edits write components.
A rejected public edit preserves the complete world. If a scheduled transform
update makes derivation invalid, local transforms return to their last accepted
values and existing derived values remain valid. Schedule administrative progress
is retained. The persistent RenderScene and incremental invalidation belong to E5.

## Description and runtime API sketch

`Creation.parent(instance, Some{index})` assigns a parent in a scene description.
`None{}` makes a root. Existing `Instance{mesh,material,transform}` remains a root.
Compilation validates relationships and derived numerical state before bootstrap.

`Scene.set_parent(app, entity, parent)` and `Scene.set_transform(app, entity, local)`
return the owned application beside an acceptance result. Invalid or stale
handles, invalid transforms, and invalid derived state return a diagnostic.
The same operations are available for the mesh application.

Version 1 JSON retains existing flat scenes. An optional `parent` is a zero-based
placement index or null. Every part of a model placement shares that placement's
local transform. Its first part is the parent anchor; remaining parts attach to
the anchor with identity local transforms. This expansion is used only for scenes
with parent links, so old flat instance order and transform behavior remain intact.
Parent references address placements before model expansion. Empty models cannot
serve as anchors. Unknown fields and invalid references remain errors.

## Acceptance and required evidence

The production path is description → Creation/JSON validation → ECS columns →
sequential derivation → detached draws → shared offscreen/window draw recording.
The hierarchy evaluator, ECS publication adapter, normal payload, and renderer
preflight enforce the contract.

Required evidence includes:

- Formal claims in `LAWS.bend` against production definitions for composition,
  rejection, publication, and bounds derivation. Numerical properties additionally
  run in native Bend with explicit tolerance and independently calculated geometry.
- Actual ECS executions covering deep chains, branches, forward references,
  movement, rotation, nonuniform scale/shear, reparenting, detachment, independent
  branches, and exact preservation after invalid edits.
- Real Vulkan RGBA/D32 readbacks against an independently transformed mesh,
  including surface-normal lighting. Owned X11 execution and deterministic replay
  compare complete local/global/bounds state, not just a digest.
- Existing flat-scene, JSON, textured rendering, mesh, and window consumers.
- Passing baseline → deliberate production regression rejected at the named
  property → restored passing baseline. A build failure is not detection evidence.
- A source-specific `verify-workflow` receipt with every required stage complete.

## Performance evaluation plan

Measure sequential publication cost and its share of real rendering workloads
for flat, deep, and branching scenes. Count accepted updates and validate final
state/output. Use five interleaved runs per comparison and report median/range.
Inspect the machine load and use a separate profiling run to identify the limiter.
Consider improvement only if propagation exceeds 2 ms per 1000-node update or
adds over 10% to a representative frame. Set a concrete target before trying a
change. Allow at most three single-change attempts, retain only repeatable gains
with identical state/render output, and validate a winner on additional scenes.
Otherwise retain the straightforward implementation. No parallelism is planned.

import Base
import ./upload-boundary/scan.bend as S
import ./verify-native-failures.bend as Native
import ./verify-upload-mutations.bend as Files

# Mutate copies of production definitions, leaving laws and proofs unchanged.
# Each rejected run must identify the expected law, not just exit nonzero.
def record(result:U32 & (String & String),+dest:String,+label:String,+failure:String) -> IO(Unit):
  (+status,pair) = result
  (out,err) = pair
  +log:String = out ++ err
  +negative:Bool = Bool.not(String.eq(failure,""))
  do IO<Unit>:
    Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ label ++ ".log",log)
    Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ label ++ ".status",U32.show(status) ++ "\n")
    S.require(Bool.pick(Bool,negative,
      U32.is_eq(status,1) && String.contains(log,"SOME PROOFS FAIL") && String.contains(log,"Location: Laws." ++ failure ++ "\n"),
      U32.is_zero(status) && String.contains(log,"ALL PROOFS CHECK")),
      "Unexpected law mutation verdict: " ++ label ++ "; see " ++ dest)
    IO.print(label ++ Bool.pick(String,negative," rejected by " ++ failure," passed"))

def gate(+dest:String,+label:String,proof:String,failure:String) -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    result:U32 & (String & String) <- IO.try(U32 & (String & String),Process.run("env",["-C",dest,"bend",proof],"",16777216,300000))
    record(result,dest,label,failure)

def mutation(+dest:String,parts:List<&2,String>) -> IO(Unit):
  match parts:
    case [+label,+path,+proof,before,after,failure]:
      do IO<Unit>:
        +original:String <- S.read(path)
        +changed:String <- Native.replaced(Native.replace(String.split(original,'\n'),before,after))
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ label ++ ".source",changed)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ path,changed)
        gate(dest,label,proof,failure)
        Files.save(dest ++ "/" ++ path,original)
    case _:IO.die(Unit,1,"Malformed Bend law mutation")

def mutations(+dest:String,lines:List<&2,String>) -> IO(Unit):
  match lines:
    case []:IO.pure(Unit,Unit{})
    case line <> rest:
      do IO<Unit>:
        mutation(dest,String.split(line,'\t'))
        mutations(dest,rest)

def main() -> IO(Unit):
  do IO<Unit>:
    _:String <- S.run("mkdir",["-p","build/verification"])
    directory:String <- S.run("mktemp",["-d","build/verification/law-mutations-XXXXXXXX"])
    +dest:String = String.trim(directory)
    IO.print("Bend law mutation evidence: " ++ dest)
    _:String <- S.run("cp",["-R","--reflink=auto","--","src","proofs","tools","examples","deps","LAWS.bend","PROOF.bend","toolchain.bend",dest])
    hashes:String <- S.run("sha256sum",["src/asset.bend","src/scene-geometry-policy.bend","src/time.bend","src/upload-size.bend","deps/bend-vulkan/src/core.bend","LAWS.bend","PROOF.bend","proofs/upload-range/LAWS.bend","proofs/upload-range/PROOF.bend","proofs/law-mutations.tsv","tools/verify-law-mutations.bend"])
    Files.save(dest ++ "/sources.sha256",hashes)
    gate(dest,"baseline-root","PROOF.bend","")
    gate(dest,"baseline-upload","proofs/upload-range/PROOF.bend","")
    cases:String <- S.read("proofs/law-mutations.tsv")
    mutations(dest,String.lines(String.trim(cases)))
    gate(dest,"restored-root","PROOF.bend","")
    gate(dest,"restored-upload","proofs/upload-range/PROOF.bend","")
    IO.print("Production Bend law mutations rejected; original sources restored in the evidence copy.")

# Public creation reference

`src/creation.bend` defines immutable scenes, instances, cameras, and compiled
ranges. Mesh and material source values come from
[`src/content.bend`](content.md). Constructors create ordinary unchecked values.
`compile(Scene)` is the checked entry point and returns
`Result<Error,Compiled>`. It needs neither Vulkan nor a window.

## Descriptions

- `Content.Vertex`, `Content.Mesh`, and `Content.Basic` follow the
  [mesh and material contract](content.md). RGB is finite but unrestricted in
  magnitude. Tint is finite and bounded to `[0,1]`.
- `Instance{mesh,material,transform}` creates one initial ECS entity.
  Translation and scale must be finite. Quaternion squared length must lie in
  `[0.9999,1.0001]`.
- `Scene{instances}` preserves instance order through compilation and bootstrap.

`compile` first rejects more than 100,000 instances with `TooLarge`. It then
validates instances in source order. Each instance reports `BadMesh` before
`BadMaterial`, then `BadTransform`, carrying the zero-based instance position.
A source mesh over the current 381,300-vertex or 3,000,000-index profile reports
`BadMesh`. A new pair that overflows aggregate packed counts reports `TooLarge`.
A duplicate pair reuses its range before any aggregate growth check. Validation
and packing complete before any GPU allocation.

Compilation materializes only used mesh/material pairs. Bitwise structural
comparison identifies identical source values. First occurrences determine
range order. Repeated pairs share a range while retaining separate ECS entities.
References start at 7 to preserve the existing demonstration's mesh reference.
Applications consume generated references instead of selecting them.

`Compiled{seeds,geometry}` is the single result. Each `Seed{transform,mesh}`
contains the existing `MeshRef`, which identifies baked geometry. It is not an
entity identity. `Geometry{vertices,indices,ranges}` contains tinted vertices,
rebased indices, and `Range{id,first_index,index_count,texture}` values.
The texture is `None` for Basic materials and `Some{SourceImage}` for textured materials.
Positions, UVs, and normals remain unchanged. `resolve(ranges,id)` returns the matching range or `None`.

`Scene.create(seeds)` registers the existing Bendvy application. The first tick
queues and publishes initial entities, then runs the existing movement system.
Bendvy handles identify entities. A second tick moves existing entities without
spawning them again. Reservation refusal retains ownership through the existing
bootstrap error path. There is no new runtime asset service or material column.

Both renderers accept `Geometry`, validate its bounds before allocating, and
preflight every extracted drawing before recording commands. They issue the
range's actual first index and count in extraction order with the existing
camera/model matrix push. Zero-index ranges issue no draw or push commands.
Geometry with no indices owns no vertex or index buffers. Framebuffer clears
and presentation still run.

## Camera

`Camera{target,yaw,pitch,distance,projection}` defines an orbit around `target`.
`Perspective{scale,near,far}` uses the vertical projection scale, equivalent to
`cot(vertical_fov / 2)`. All values must be finite. Distance, scale, and near
must be positive, and far must exceed near.

`camera(value)` returns `Some` for a valid configuration and `None` otherwise.
`view(camera,width,height)` returns a finite matrix or `None`. Invalid cameras,
zero dimensions, and non-finite derived matrices return `None`.
`default_camera()` preserves the old orbit and projection arithmetic. The demo
applies its own tick-one framing separately.

`Input.key` changes orbit values while preserving target and projection. Reset
restores yaw `0.65`, pitch `0.45`, and distance `7.0`, preserving the configured
target and lens. Reset does not restore a caller's custom initial orbit.
Controls retain the existing pitch clamp `[0.1,1.4]` and distance clamp `[4,15]`.

## Startup callbacks

The four slots in `src/modules.bend` have these concrete inputs and outputs:

| Slot | Callback |
| --- | --- |
| `Core<A>` | `List<Seed> -> IO(A)` |
| `Input` | `Unit -> Camera` |
| `Assets` | `Unit -> Scene` |
| `Render` | `V.Entry -> Geometry -> V.Action(Win.Renderer)` |

The existing executable calls Assets once, compiles once, sends its geometry to
Render, and sends the same result's seeds to Core. Core retains responsibility
for its first tick. The example recipe owns the former fixed 100-entity seeds.
Render adapters are engine assembly code and retain Vulkan access. The public
creation example imports no Vulkan module and handles no Vulkan values.

## Scope

Creation supplies startup entities and packed renderer geometry. Both renderers
support [whole-mesh replacement](mesh-replacement.md), including deferred destruction
and preservation on rejected candidates. [Textured materials](textured-materials.md)
use the same geometry and camera APIs. Runtime entity insertion, per-asset deletion,
transparency, and persistent GPU scene storage remain separate work.
Packing uses sequential structural lookup for small startup scenes. No
performance or cross-backend bitwise determinism claim is made.

The [verification record](verification/2026-11-03-public-creation/README.md)
records formal claims, real ECS execution, offscreen rendering, and X11 captures.
# Scene state ownership

The retained `Scene.Application()` owns the authoritative component state through
its Bendvy world. Future simulation chunks must be storage owned by that world,
with exclusive access transferred to a numerical task and returned afterward.
They cannot be an independently writable mirror of ECS components.

This contract completes the E2 ownership decision. Entangle has no simulation
chunk implementation or chunk transfer API yet. R0 must establish which storage
operations the pinned Bend toolchain and Bendvy can support.

## Authoritative state and observations

For each live entity and component, one storage owner determines the next
authoritative value. Several systems can update that storage in schedule order.
A single owner does not mean that only one system may ever write a component.

| Representation | Authority |
| --- | --- |
| `Scene.Application()` and its `D.World()` | Retain component storage, allocator, deferred commands, and schedule state. |
| Registered `GeneralWriter` and its execution scope `H` | Authorize an update of the current component in that world. The operation consumes and returns the scope. |
| `C.Transform`, query row views, and `Observe.Snapshot` | Copyable values. They carry no scope or writer and cannot publish themselves. |
| `Draw.DrawList` | Detached rendering input. It has neither entity handles nor a component writer. |
| Future owned simulation chunks | A partition of authoritative storage while tasks hold it. Ordinary ECS access to that partition must be unavailable until ownership returns. |
| Future halos, neighbor snapshots, and render projections | Derived read inputs with a defined observation phase. They do not authorize component replacement. |

`World`, the retained application state, and the schedule wrapper have kind
`Type`. Bend's affine checker prevents reusing the same owner. Component records
have kind `Data`, so copying a transform remains legal and useful.

Affinity alone does not establish this contract. Two separately allocated affine
arrays can contain independently evolving copies of the same components. A
component handle also identifies an entity without granting access to its storage.

## Current write path

[`scene-schema.bend`](../src/scene-schema.bend) registers ordinary `Transform` and
`MeshRef` columns. Its payload-to-view projections copy values for observation.
They do not transfer component storage to the reader.

[`scene.bend`](../src/scene.bend) retains the world inside `Scene.Application()`.
`Scene.run` consumes that application and returns its successor with a schedule
report. Bootstrap publishes initial components before the movement system runs.

[`scene-motion.bend`](../src/scene-motion.bend) requests a `WriteRows` capability
for transforms on entities with `MeshRef`. `move_rows` uses the selected handle
and discards the row's copied transform. `GeneralWriter.modify` supplies the
current stored transform to `translate`, which calls `Step.step` and returns the
replacement. Each call returns the scope used by the next row.

Calling `Step.step` on a snapshot calculates a detached value. It does not update
the scene. Production movement has no snapshot-to-world writeback operation.
Later systems must also update through the owner instead of installing values
computed from an earlier observation without an explicit conflict policy.

Numerical writes are immediate. A refused query returns the incoming scope.
A refused write stops movement and retains earlier accepted writes. Structural
commands publish at the schedule's apply boundaries. Ownership transfer must not
silently turn these operations into an atomic batch or add rollback. See the
[headless reference](headless-reference.md) and
[schedule visibility contract](schedule-visibility.md).

[`scene-observe.bend`](../src/scene-observe.bend) consumes and reconstructs the
application around a read-only inspector. Snapshots and drawing data may outlive
the observation. Rendering or replaying them cannot restore an older scene.

## Future chunk integration

The selected model keeps ECS as the persistent owner. Chunk layout is an internal
storage choice. A work batch describes computation over that storage and need
not have the same boundaries as a storage chunk.

A future transfer API must represent these conditions in its types and checked
operations before production simulation uses it:

1. The simulation adapter consumes the owner or an exclusive storage capability.
   Partitioning transfers payload ownership. It does not clone canonical fields
   into a second persistent container.
2. Each task receives exclusive access to its assigned partition. Partition
   membership covers the selected entities without overlap. Entity handles retain
   their namespace and generation and do not become unchecked physical indexes.
3. While tasks hold partitions, the remaining coordinator cannot obtain an ECS
   reader or writer for those partitions. A usable world and writable detached
   chunks must never coexist for the same components.
4. Cross-partition reads use a specified read-only representation, such as a
   bounded snapshot from tick start. That representation carries no writeback
   permission. Its phase and copy costs are part of the algorithm's contract.
5. Completion returns each owned partition through the same adapter before
   ordinary ECS access and extraction resume. A refused or cancelled operation
   must account for every partition and define the resulting authoritative state.
6. Structural changes that invalidate partition membership or storage addresses
   wait for ownership to return. Their publication order follows the explicit
   schedule contract. Render extraction observes a completed state boundary.

These are requirements for a future API, not descriptions of a shipped lease or
split operation. The pinned dependency's `chunk-column.Column` is an affine
storage implementation. Its existence does not establish a safe Entangle task
handoff. If exclusive transfer cannot be expressed, simulation remains sequential
through the current ECS writer. Independently allocated chunks may be canonical
storage if the world owns them without retaining writable duplicate columns.

R0 may run a standalone numerical reference from copied initial values. That is
a separate execution for comparison, not a live mirror with a writeback path.
CPU or GPU dispatch changes execution only. The ownership and numerical contract
must remain the same without GPU dispatch.

## Excluded designs and trusted boundary

A permanent ECS store plus a mutable simulation mirror violates this contract,
even if a scheduler runs their writers sequentially or synchronizes them every
frame. The contract also excludes restoring a retained draw list, snapshot, or
neighbor halo as current component state.

Moving persistent authority outside ECS would require a separate design change.
That change must remove writable ECS storage for those fields, expose derived
read projections, and route edits as commands to the simulation owner. A second
store cannot be introduced as an incremental compatibility path.

Trusted provisioning code can construct raw world records and register writers.
The current public Bendvy constructors do not make this repository an opaque
capability sandbox. The contract constrains those callers too. The affine checker
prevents owner reuse, but it does not forbid an engineer from adding a new store.
Future chunk integration therefore needs production-path ownership checks and
must remove any duplicate writer path in the same change.

## Verification and limits

`LAWS.bend` states general claims against the current production adapter:

- `scene_move_view_independent` proves that substituting any optional head-row
  view leaves traversal unchanged for arbitrary remaining rows and scope.
- `scene_move_current_component` proves that traversal passes `Move.translate`
  to the supplied writer for that handle, then continues with the returned scope.
- `scene_move_query_refusal` proves that a refused query returns the incoming
  scope with the query error and does not call the writer.
- `scene_step_adapter` binds that callback to the numerical kernel. Existing
  kernel laws specify its translation, preserved rotation and scale, and output.

`PROOF.bend` checks these claims. They assume the supplied writer's contract and
do not prove every Bendvy storage operation or prevent future duplicate stores.
The native verifier exercises the actual registered writer across eight ticks,
checks every entity's identity and transform, and checks detached render replay.

```sh
bend PROOF.bend
bend tools/verify.bend
```

The [verification record](verification/2026-11-03-state-ownership/README.md)
records the runs and their limits. R0 and R1 still need checks for partition
coverage, unavailable competing writers, ownership return on failure, and
equivalence with the sequential reference. No future chunk implementation is
proved by the current adapter laws.

# Public creation reference

`src/creation.bend` defines immutable scenes, instances, cameras, and compiled
ranges. Mesh and material source values come from
[`src/content.bend`](content.md). Constructors create ordinary unchecked values.
`compile(Scene)` is the checked entry point and returns
`Result<Error,Compiled>`. It needs neither Vulkan nor a window.

## Descriptions

- `Content.Vertex`, `Content.Mesh`, and `Content.Basic` follow the
  [mesh and material contract](content.md). RGB is finite but unrestricted in
  magnitude. Tint is finite and bounded to `[0,1]`.
- `Instance{mesh,material,transform}` creates one initial ECS entity.
  Translation and scale must be finite. Quaternion squared length must lie in
  `[0.9999,1.0001]`.
- `Scene{instances}` preserves instance order through compilation and bootstrap.

`compile` first rejects more than 100,000 instances with `TooLarge`. It then
validates instances in source order. Each instance reports `BadMesh` before
`BadMaterial`, then `BadTransform`, carrying the zero-based instance position.
A source mesh over the current 381,300-vertex or 3,000,000-index profile reports
`BadMesh`. A new pair that overflows aggregate packed counts reports `TooLarge`.
A duplicate pair reuses its range before any aggregate growth check. Validation
and packing complete before any GPU allocation.

Compilation materializes only used mesh/material pairs. Bitwise structural
comparison identifies identical source values. First occurrences determine
range order. Repeated pairs share a range while retaining separate ECS entities.
References start at 7 to preserve the existing demonstration's mesh reference.
Applications consume generated references instead of selecting them.

`Compiled{seeds,geometry}` is the single result. Each `Seed{transform,mesh}`
contains the existing `MeshRef`, which identifies baked geometry. It is not an
entity identity. `Geometry{vertices,indices,ranges}` contains tinted vertices,
rebased indices, and `Range{id,first_index,index_count,texture}` values.
The texture is `None` for Basic materials and `Some{SourceImage}` for textured materials.
Positions, UVs, and normals remain unchanged. `resolve(ranges,id)` returns the matching range or `None`.

`Scene.create(seeds)` registers the existing Bendvy application. The first tick
queues and publishes initial entities, then runs the existing movement system.
Bendvy handles identify entities. A second tick moves existing entities without
spawning them again. Reservation refusal retains ownership through the existing
bootstrap error path. There is no new runtime asset service or material column.

Both renderers accept `Geometry`, validate its bounds before allocating, and
preflight every extracted drawing before recording commands. They issue the
range's actual first index and count in extraction order with the existing
camera/model matrix push. Zero-index ranges issue no draw or push commands.
Geometry with no indices owns no vertex or index buffers. Framebuffer clears
and presentation still run.

## Camera

`Camera{target,yaw,pitch,distance,projection}` defines an orbit around `target`.
`Perspective{scale,near,far}` uses the vertical projection scale, equivalent to
`cot(vertical_fov / 2)`. All values must be finite. Distance, scale, and near
must be positive, and far must exceed near.

`camera(value)` returns `Some` for a valid configuration and `None` otherwise.
`view(camera,width,height)` returns a finite matrix or `None`. Invalid cameras,
zero dimensions, and non-finite derived matrices return `None`.
`default_camera()` preserves the old orbit and projection arithmetic. The demo
applies its own tick-one framing separately.

`Input.key` changes orbit values while preserving target and projection. Reset
restores yaw `0.65`, pitch `0.45`, and distance `7.0`, preserving the configured
target and lens. Reset does not restore a caller's custom initial orbit.
Controls retain the existing pitch clamp `[0.1,1.4]` and distance clamp `[4,15]`.

## Startup callbacks

The four slots in `src/modules.bend` have these concrete inputs and outputs:

| Slot | Callback |
| --- | --- |
| `Core<A>` | `List<Seed> -> IO(A)` |
| `Input` | `Unit -> Camera` |
| `Assets` | `Unit -> Scene` |
| `Render` | `V.Entry -> Geometry -> V.Action(Win.Renderer)` |

The existing executable calls Assets once, compiles once, sends its geometry to
Render, and sends the same result's seeds to Core. Core retains responsibility
for its first tick. The example recipe owns the former fixed 100-entity seeds.
Render adapters are engine assembly code and retain Vulkan access. The public
creation example imports no Vulkan module and handles no Vulkan values.

## Scope

Creation supplies startup entities and packed renderer geometry. Both renderers
support [whole-mesh replacement](mesh-replacement.md), including deferred destruction
and preservation on rejected candidates. [Textured materials](textured-materials.md)
use the same geometry and camera APIs. Runtime entity insertion, per-asset deletion,
transparency, and persistent GPU scene storage remain separate work.
Packing uses sequential structural lookup for small startup scenes. No
performance or cross-backend bitwise determinism claim is made.

The [verification record](verification/2026-11-03-public-creation/README.md)
records formal claims, real ECS execution, offscreen rendering, and X11 captures.
# Scene state ownership

The retained `Scene.Application()` owns the authoritative component state through
its Bendvy world. Future simulation chunks must be storage owned by that world,
with exclusive access transferred to a numerical task and returned afterward.
They cannot be an independently writable mirror of ECS components.

This contract completes the E2 ownership decision. Entangle has no simulation
chunk implementation or chunk transfer API yet. R0 must establish which storage
operations the pinned Bend toolchain and Bendvy can support.

## Authoritative state and observations

For each live entity and component, one storage owner determines the next
authoritative value. Several systems can update that storage in schedule order.
A single owner does not mean that only one system may ever write a component.

| Representation | Authority |
| --- | --- |
| `Scene.Application()` and its `D.World()` | Retain component storage, allocator, deferred commands, and schedule state. |
| Registered `GeneralWriter` and its execution scope `H` | Authorize an update of the current component in that world. The operation consumes and returns the scope. |
| `C.Transform`, query row views, and `Observe.Snapshot` | Copyable values. They carry no scope or writer and cannot publish themselves. |
| `Draw.DrawList` | Detached rendering input. It has neither entity handles nor a component writer. |
| Future owned simulation chunks | A partition of authoritative storage while tasks hold it. Ordinary ECS access to that partition must be unavailable until ownership returns. |
| Future halos, neighbor snapshots, and render projections | Derived read inputs with a defined observation phase. They do not authorize component replacement. |

`World`, the retained application state, and the schedule wrapper have kind
`Type`. Bend's affine checker prevents reusing the same owner. Component records
have kind `Data`, so copying a transform remains legal and useful.

Affinity alone does not establish this contract. Two separately allocated affine
arrays can contain independently evolving copies of the same components. A
component handle also identifies an entity without granting access to its storage.

## Current write path

[`scene-schema.bend`](../src/scene-schema.bend) registers ordinary `Transform` and
`MeshRef` columns. Its payload-to-view projections copy values for observation.
They do not transfer component storage to the reader.

[`scene.bend`](../src/scene.bend) retains the world inside `Scene.Application()`.
`Scene.run` consumes that application and returns its successor with a schedule
report. Bootstrap publishes initial components before the movement system runs.

[`scene-motion.bend`](../src/scene-motion.bend) requests a `WriteRows` capability
for transforms on entities with `MeshRef`. `move_rows` uses the selected handle
and discards the row's copied transform. `GeneralWriter.modify` supplies the
current stored transform to `translate`, which calls `Step.step` and returns the
replacement. Each call returns the scope used by the next row.

Calling `Step.step` on a snapshot calculates a detached value. It does not update
the scene. Production movement has no snapshot-to-world writeback operation.
Later systems must also update through the owner instead of installing values
computed from an earlier observation without an explicit conflict policy.

Numerical writes are immediate. A refused query returns the incoming scope.
A refused write stops movement and retains earlier accepted writes. Structural
commands publish at the schedule's apply boundaries. Ownership transfer must not
silently turn these operations into an atomic batch or add rollback. See the
[headless reference](headless-reference.md) and
[schedule visibility contract](schedule-visibility.md).

[`scene-observe.bend`](../src/scene-observe.bend) consumes and reconstructs the
application around a read-only inspector. Snapshots and drawing data may outlive
the observation. Rendering or replaying them cannot restore an older scene.

## Future chunk integration

The selected model keeps ECS as the persistent owner. Chunk layout is an internal
storage choice. A work batch describes computation over that storage and need
not have the same boundaries as a storage chunk.

A future transfer API must represent these conditions in its types and checked
operations before production simulation uses it:

1. The simulation adapter consumes the owner or an exclusive storage capability.
   Partitioning transfers payload ownership. It does not clone canonical fields
   into a second persistent container.
2. Each task receives exclusive access to its assigned partition. Partition
   membership covers the selected entities without overlap. Entity handles retain
   their namespace and generation and do not become unchecked physical indexes.
3. While tasks hold partitions, the remaining coordinator cannot obtain an ECS
   reader or writer for those partitions. A usable world and writable detached
   chunks must never coexist for the same components.
4. Cross-partition reads use a specified read-only representation, such as a
   bounded snapshot from tick start. That representation carries no writeback
   permission. Its phase and copy costs are part of the algorithm's contract.
5. Completion returns each owned partition through the same adapter before
   ordinary ECS access and extraction resume. A refused or cancelled operation
   must account for every partition and define the resulting authoritative state.
6. Structural changes that invalidate partition membership or storage addresses
   wait for ownership to return. Their publication order follows the explicit
   schedule contract. Render extraction observes a completed state boundary.

These are requirements for a future API, not descriptions of a shipped lease or
split operation. The pinned dependency's `chunk-column.Column` is an affine
storage implementation. Its existence does not establish a safe Entangle task
handoff. If exclusive transfer cannot be expressed, simulation remains sequential
through the current ECS writer. Independently allocated chunks may be canonical
storage if the world owns them without retaining writable duplicate columns.

R0 may run a standalone numerical reference from copied initial values. That is
a separate execution for comparison, not a live mirror with a writeback path.
CPU or GPU dispatch changes execution only. The ownership and numerical contract
must remain the same without GPU dispatch.

## Excluded designs and trusted boundary

A permanent ECS store plus a mutable simulation mirror violates this contract,
even if a scheduler runs their writers sequentially or synchronizes them every
frame. The contract also excludes restoring a retained draw list, snapshot, or
neighbor halo as current component state.

Moving persistent authority outside ECS would require a separate design change.
That change must remove writable ECS storage for those fields, expose derived
read projections, and route edits as commands to the simulation owner. A second
store cannot be introduced as an incremental compatibility path.

Trusted provisioning code can construct raw world records and register writers.
The current public Bendvy constructors do not make this repository an opaque
capability sandbox. The contract constrains those callers too. The affine checker
prevents owner reuse, but it does not forbid an engineer from adding a new store.
Future chunk integration therefore needs production-path ownership checks and
must remove any duplicate writer path in the same change.

## Verification and limits

`LAWS.bend` states general claims against the current production adapter:

- `scene_move_view_independent` proves that substituting any optional head-row
  view leaves traversal unchanged for arbitrary remaining rows and scope.
- `scene_move_current_component` proves that traversal passes `Move.translate`
  to the supplied writer for that handle, then continues with the returned scope.
- `scene_move_query_refusal` proves that a refused query returns the incoming
  scope with the query error and does not call the writer.
- `scene_step_adapter` binds that callback to the numerical kernel. Existing
  kernel laws specify its translation, preserved rotation and scale, and output.

`PROOF.bend` checks these claims. They assume the supplied writer's contract and
do not prove every Bendvy storage operation or prevent future duplicate stores.
The native verifier exercises the actual registered writer across eight ticks,
checks every entity's identity and transform, and checks detached render replay.

```sh
bend PROOF.bend
bend tools/verify.bend
```

The [verification record](verification/2026-11-03-state-ownership/README.md)
records the runs and their limits. R0 and R1 still need checks for partition
coverage, unavailable competing writers, ownership return on failure, and
equivalence with the sequential reference. No future chunk implementation is
proved by the current adapter laws.

# JSON scene files and manifests

`SceneFile.load(path)` reads a flat scene, resolves its manifest, validates every
declared OBJ and PNG source, and returns `Creation.Scene`. Errors are
`Asset.Error` values. Loading creates no ECS or Vulkan resources. The caller can
cache the result through `Asset.load` and compile it through `Creation.compile`.

```python
import ./src/scene-file.bend as SceneFile

def load(path:String) -> IO(Result<&2,&2,Asset.Error,Creation.Scene>)
def load_manifest(path:String) -> IO(Result<&2,&2,Asset.Error,List<&2,SceneFile.Source>>)
```

`load_manifest` returns ordered `ModelSource{id,value}` and
`ImageSource{id,value}` entries after all declared files load successfully.
`decode_manifest(bytes,path)` and `decode_scene(bytes,path)` validate JSON into
`Manifest` and `Description` without file access. Their `path` argument supplies
diagnostic context. `load` additionally resolves references and checks that the
result compiles through the existing Creation rules. No partial scene is
returned on failure.

## Version 1 schema

Every listed field is required. Unknown fields and wrong types are errors at
all object levels. Object field order is irrelevant. Array order is preserved.
Version is the exact JSON integer token `1`.

A manifest has this shape.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "assets": [
    {"id": "sign", "kind": "obj", "path": "sign.obj"},
    {"id": "image", "kind": "png", "path": "image.png"}
  ]
}
```

A scene has this shape.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "manifest": "manifest.json",
  "instances": [
    {
      "model": "sign",
      "transform": {
        "position": [0, 0, 0],
        "rotation": [0, 0, 0, 1],
        "scale": [1, 1, 1]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

IDs contain 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores. They are
case-sensitive and unique across both asset kinds. Each scene model reference
must name an OBJ entry. A PNG entry cannot be used as a model. Every declared
asset loads, including unused entries. Missing files and malformed OBJ, MTL,
or PNG contents fail the load.

The manifest path is relative to the scene file. Each asset path is relative
to the manifest file. Paths contain printable ASCII slash-separated components.
Empty components, `.` and `..`, backslashes, colons, spaces, and control bytes
are rejected. These are lexical path rules. They do not confine symlink targets
or provide a filesystem sandbox. Root paths must be nonempty, contain no NUL,
and fit within 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Joined paths have the same limit.

A model's parts expand in order at each placement. Meshes, materials, winding,
and transforms are preserved. Existing Creation compilation shares identical
mesh/material pairs. Images remain source assets. This schema adds no texture
binding, cameras, parent hierarchy, animation, or new model format.

## Parser and limits

Both document kinds use only `bend-kit-json@0.7.0.0`, content hash
`0x37aacddc1dcb57464b8b5ac6c397bd64`, through
`parse.strict.unique.bytes`. Its byte storage is
`bend-kit-bytes@0.3.3.0`, hash `0x632652e3c1c0183f12728faf3870bb68`.
Strict UTF-8, complete JSON consumption, valid escapes, and unique decoded
object keys are required. Duplicate keys are rejected even when written with
different escape spellings. Neither first nor last duplicate wins.

The parser retains numeric tokens exactly. Version validation uses that text.
Transform values use `F32.read` only after JSON syntax validation and a numeric
token length check. The resulting F32 must be finite and within
`[-1000000,1000000]`. Decimal values round to F32, including underflow to signed
zero. Position and scale contain exactly three numbers. Rotation contains
exactly four numbers in x/y/z/w order. Its squared norm must be within
`[0.9999,1.0001]`. Loading does not normalize it. Zero and negative scale remain
valid under the existing Creation contract.

| Boundary | Limit |
| --- | --- |

# Verify Entangle

Read [the feature map](features/README.md) first. Entangle's primary interactive app is a native X11 window. Its other user paths are Bend scene descriptions and command-line examples. There is no web server, account, database, or seed service. Examples supply their own scene data.

For formal verification maintenance, follow [the law checks](features/formal-laws.md).
That entry records covered code, assumptions, commands, mutation controls, and
the synchronization commit separately from live-window evidence.

## Select required evidence

Follow [the development workflow](../../../docs/development.md). Create `build` with `mkdir -p build`, run `bend tools/verify-workflow.bend -o build/verify-workflow`, inspect `./build/verify-workflow --plan PROFILE...`, then execute the affected profiles. The runner retains a source snapshot, commands, per-stage statuses and logs. Required failures and unexecuted stages cannot produce a passing receipt. Read the feature map for scenarios outside the profiles.

Keep one implementation owner. For a new critical verifier, establish sensitivity to the named production defect and restore the baseline. Use a focused independent check only for a concrete uncertainty about the oracle, bounds, or production correspondence; no automatic adversarial panel.

## Launch

Run from the repository root on Linux x86-64. Read `AGENTS.md`, run `bend guide`, and check `toolchain.bend`. The current native lane requires Bend 2.0.39, Clang 23.1.4, Node.js or Bun, initialized dependencies, Vulkan and X11 development headers, and a Vulkan graphics/presentation device. The live recipe also needs `Xwayland`, a working parent Wayland session, and `VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation`.

Inspect dependencies with `git submodule status --recursive`. If they are missing, use the README's initialization commands. Stop on a build or startup failure and retain its logs. Do not treat a headless pass as a window pass.

The executable launcher contains the complete mesh verification lifecycle. It builds fresh executables, starts an owned rootful Xwayland, runs the doctor, drives the app, replays both traces, and cleans up. Each invocation prints its evidence path. Allow several minutes for compilation.

The isolated working directory redirects the drivers' historical output paths into fresh evidence. Never symlink its `docs` directory to the repository's real `docs`. Never replace the repository's `build/indexed-window` with the mesh executable.

```bash
bash tools/verify-window-session.sh
```

The display number file signals Xwayland readiness. The Bend driver then locates only its child's window by PID and waits for a populated 640×480 frame. Its first capture must contain all four mesh materials. A blank window or a live process alone is insufficient.

This recipe uses the existing helper's unauthenticated X11 TCP connection on a disposable display. Do not redirect it to the user's display. Independent runs have distinct display numbers and directories. Repository-wide gates that write fixed `build` paths must run sequentially.

## Doctor

The launcher runs `doctor` before input. Run it again from the launch shell whenever ownership looks wrong. It is one read-only check of the owned display process, display number, TCP port, evidence destination, and exact executable bytes. `doctor.log` records its result. A failed check means stop and run cleanup. The live driver's populated-frame and validation checks establish renderer health after launch.

For a CPU-only invocation, check `bend version`, `clang --version`, `clang -dumpmachine`, and `git submodule status` instead. Do not require a display for headless verification.

## Drive

Use the existing Bend drivers. The launch recipe runs the [mesh movement](features/mesh-movement.md) path with trace logging and also exercises the mesh entry of [camera and window controls](features/camera-window.md). Each driver starts and reaps its own application. Do not start an extra interactive copy for it to discover.

`verify-mesh-window` sends held movement edges through the actual X11 keyboard map, uses `bend-ui-test` for taps and Close, captures real window pixels, and checks cleanup. `replay-mesh-window` executes the recorded input and ticks against the real ECS application and compares full identities and transform bits. Compile these drivers natively. The default runner has previously hit a stack fault on a large trace.

Run every relevant entry in the feature map for a change. One mesh run does not cover the cube window, public creation, headless batching, or offscreen depth rendering. The feature files give their commands and expected results.

## Evidence

Keep the printed `build/verification/entangle-XXXXXXXX` directory after teardown. It contains commands, per-stage exit codes, revision and source hashes, fresh binaries, compiler and dependency information, window captures, input/state traces, replay results, and cleanup status. This directory is gitignored. Link the exact path in your report. Copy selected evidence elsewhere only when requested, and preserve the originals.

Require `run.status` and each executed stage's `.status` to be zero. Inspect `window.log` for all six `player-axis=... held=moved release=stable Space=exact` lines and the focus, resize, and exit results. Both native logs must report `Mesh playground closed; live Vulkan objects: 0` without `Validation Error`, `SYNC-HAZARD`, or `VUID-` diagnostics. Both replay logs must report real ECS replay matches. Inspect `initial.ppm`, `held.ppm`, and `reset.ppm` with an image viewer. The initial and reset files must compare byte-for-byte.

Capture the action as well as its result. A screenshot alone does not prove input, and digest equality alone does not prove world equality. Preserve the real input/state logs and successful replay checks. Verify written captures and resource cleanup alongside the visible state. Do not introduce mocks or example-based unit tests. Formal claims belong in `LAWS.bend`, with proofs in `PROOF.bend`.

`ENTANGLE_MESH_EVIDENCE=1` enables logging. It is not a dry-run: the application still opens a window, consumes input, runs ECS ticks, and allocates Vulkan resources. Report ordinary untraced execution separately if you run it. Report skipped paths and failed attempts explicitly. This recipe makes no performance, other-backend, or device-loss recovery claim.

## Cleanup

The launch block's EXIT trap runs on success and failure. Normal driver exits reap the application through the existing bridge. Its `atexit` handler kills only its owned child on assertion failure. The bounded `timeout` kills its command process group if a driver hangs. Such a run fails and cannot establish clean Vulkan shutdown.

The trap stops and reaps only the Xwayland PID it started, then deletes only the fresh runtime directory. It retains binaries, logs, traces, captures, and status files in the evidence directory. The launcher in `tools/verify-window-session.sh` builds and orchestrates the existing Bend drivers. Their invocations appear above and in the feature map. Keep verification behavior in those Bend drivers. Use `/maintain-verification-skill` when controls, paths, or observable results change.

Qualify an unfamiliar dependency with a small real input and an independently known output before designing the adapter. Keep that probe and its pinned dependency revision.

A failed check means stop and run cleanup. The live driver's populated-frame and validation checks establish renderer health after launch.

For a CPU-only invocation, check `bend version`, `clang --version`, `clang -dumpmachine`, and `git submodule status` instead. Do not require a display for headless verification.

## Drive

Use the existing Bend drivers. The launch recipe runs the [mesh movement](features/mesh-movement.md) path with trace logging and also exercises the mesh entry of [camera and window controls](features/camera-window.md). Each driver starts and reaps its own application. Do not start an extra interactive copy for it to discover.

`verify-mesh-window` sends held movement edges through the actual X11 keyboard map, uses `bend-ui-test` for taps and Close, captures real window pixels, and checks cleanup. `replay-mesh-window` executes the recorded input and ticks against the real ECS application and compares full identities and transform bits. Compile these drivers natively. The default runner has previously hit a stack fault on a large trace.

Run every relevant entry in the feature map for a change. One mesh run does not cover the cube window, public creation, headless batching, or offscreen depth rendering. The feature files give their commands and expected results.

## Evidence

Keep the printed `build/verification/entangle-XXXXXXXX` directory after teardown. It contains commands, per-stage exit codes, revision and source hashes, fresh binaries, compiler and dependency information, window captures, input/state traces, replay results, and cleanup status. This directory is gitignored. Link the exact path in your report. Copy selected evidence elsewhere only when requested, and preserve the originals.

Require `run.status` and each executed stage's `.status` to be zero. Inspect `window.log` for all six `player-axis=... held=moved release=stable Space=exact` lines and the focus, resize, and exit results. Both native logs must report `Mesh playground closed; live Vulkan objects: 0` without `Validation Error`, `SYNC-HAZARD`, or `VUID-` diagnostics. Both replay logs must report real ECS replay matches. Inspect `initial.ppm`, `held.ppm`, and `reset.ppm` with an image viewer. The initial and reset files must compare byte-for-byte.

Capture the action as well as its result. A screenshot alone does not prove input, and digest equality alone does not prove world equality. Preserve the real input/state logs and successful replay checks. Verify written captures and resource cleanup alongside the visible state. Do not introduce mocks or example-based unit tests. Formal claims belong in `LAWS.bend`, with proofs in `PROOF.bend`.

`ENTANGLE_MESH_EVIDENCE=1` enables logging. It is not a dry-run: the application still opens a window, consumes input, runs ECS ticks, and allocates Vulkan resources. ## Cleanup

The launch block's EXIT trap runs on success and failure. Normal driver exits reap the application through the existing bridge. Its `atexit` handler kills only its owned child on assertion failure. The bounded `timeout` kills its command process group if a driver hangs. Such a run fails and cannot establish clean Vulkan shutdown.

The trap stops and reaps only the Xwayland PID it started, then deletes only the fresh runtime directory. It retains binaries, logs, traces, captures, and status files in the evidence directory. Never kill by process name or remove the evidence directory to clean up. After a failed attempt, finish cleanup before starting a new run with a new evidence directory.

After the launch shell exits, inspect `cleanup.log` and `run.status` at the printed path. Confirm the runtime directory named in `cleanup.log` is absent and the recorded display PID is gone. The launcher in `tools/verify-window-session.sh` builds and orchestrates the existing Bend drivers. Their invocations appear above and in the feature map. Keep verification behavior in those Bend drivers. Use `/maintain-verification-skill` when controls, paths, or observable results change.

Keep one owner for coupled production code, laws, and verification. Ordinary features and refactors do not require architect, arena, or adversarial-review panels. Delegate a bounded independent probe only when it answers a named uncertainty. Model-role configuration does not require a panel.

## Before implementation

In the existing task or Trail, record the observable outcome, the production functions that enforce it, the required checks, and their limits. Qualify an unfamiliar dependency with a small real input and an independently known output before designing the adapter. Keep that probe and its pinned dependency revision.

Use real files and native consumers for effects. Prove important general properties against production definitions. For rare driver results that cannot reliably be induced by valid runtime inputs, state the symbolic boundary and bounded proof scope in advance. Preserve the distinction between Bend frontend checks, kernel verdicts, bounded CBMC proofs, and observed hardware behavior.

A new or changed critical verifier needs a sensitivity control. The original implementation passes, a deliberate production-source regression violates the named property, and restored sources pass. A timeout, compiler crash, parse error, or unrelated rejection does not establish sensitivity. Fix the verifier when its oracle is wrong; do not weaken the production contract to make it green.

## 1. Project boundaries

### What “an engine in Bend” means

App, systems and ECS integration, scenes, transforms, resource management, game logic, draw-data extraction, and pass planning live in Bend. New engine algorithms are also written in Bend by default.

The native layer handles the ABI, system calls, driver objects, and boundary protection. Visibility determination, game-scene management, material selection, and the pass dependency graph are not moved into it.

Existing defensive checks in the C backend are retained. They should not be removed before a verified replacement exists. The existing GLSL → SPIR-V path remains an explicitly identified GPU-code boundary; a custom Bend shader compiler is not an alpha requirement [S1, S2].

# Entangle verification map

Read this index before choosing checks. Each file maps user actions to existing Bend drivers and observable results. The map describes coverage to run, not a claim that every path passed in the latest session.

## Baseline preconditions

- Run from the repository root with the toolchain and dependency revisions in `toolchain.bend`.
- Use the skill's fresh runtime and owned display for native window checks. Drivers find only their own child window.
- Run the doctor before input. Preserve evidence outside disposable runtime state.
- Run gates that write fixed repository `build` paths sequentially. Do not drive or terminate another session's app.
- Read `AGENTS.md`. Use formal laws, real runtime checks, and live input/replay evidence. Add no unit tests or mocks.

## Driving conventions

The executable `tools/verify-window-session.sh` launcher drives mesh movement. For additional camera-window scenarios, follow that feature recipe with its own owned display and runtime. CPU and offscreen recipes are independent shell invocations. They create their own evidence directory and exit after the real process returns.

For an optional window block, copy `tools/verify-window-session.sh` into the ignored `build/verification` directory, insert the block before its `run window ...` command, and run that copy from the repository root. Keep the copied script with the evidence. Do not edit the shared launcher or run the block after its display has been cleaned up.

Use the exact key symbols and native driver modes in the feature files. Do not infer desktop coverage from a headless run. Do not reuse archived captures as evidence for a new build.

## Proof and skip reporting

Record the feature ID, entry point, command, output, exit status, and resulting state. For UI changes, retain captures, native action/state traces where available, and zero-object shutdown logs. For file output, inspect the resulting file. Report build failures and missing display, validation layer, or device prerequisites explicitly.

A mesh pass covers the mesh entry of camera controls. It does not establish the cube entry. A creation CLI pass does not establish rendered colors or depth. If a change affects multiple entries, run all affected entries or list those skipped.

## Features

Use the [verification profiles](../../../../docs/development.md#run-verification) to select required checks. Profile success is scoped to its listed scenarios.

- [Formal laws](formal-laws.md): production Bend definitions, the universal upload-range theorem, mutation controls, and synchronization records.
- [S41 math qualification](../../../../docs/verification/2026-11-05-jonmath/README.md): explicit candidate adapters, numerical contracts, sensitivity controls, and exact retained scene comparisons through the `math` profile.
- [Source assets](../../../../docs/assets.md#verification-and-limits): typed cache handles, real file loading, cached failures, release/retry, exact retained mesh and material sources, source-only dependency closure, and scene execution after source release.
- [PNG source images](images.md): pinned decoder, retained real images, complete-pixel comparison, file/cache/retry behavior and production mutation controls.
- [Static OBJ sources](models.md): pinned parser, exact mesh/material/label conversion, file/cache/retry, source-only closure, real ECS/offscreen geometry, and owned X11 culling evidence.
- [JSON scene files and manifests](json-scene.md): one pinned parser, strict schema and reference validation, bounded loading, cache/retry, source preservation, and real ECS/offscreen evidence.
- [Checked host uploads](upload-boundary.md): enforced source policy, exact production payload lengths, real Vulkan writes and readback, rejection, and cleanup.
- [Mesh replacement](mesh-replacement.md): both renderer APIs, changed pixels and ranges, rejected-candidate preservation, recorded commands, multiple submissions, uniform and sampled-image descriptor retention, memory aliases, atomic retirement rejection, collection, and cleanup.
- [Native resource failures](resource-failures.md): recording/submission/reset rejection, real allocation failure under a process limit, partial preparation rollback, cleanup diagnostics, terminal teardown, and bounded proofs of production handlers for rare driver errors.
- [Mesh movement](mesh-movement.md): six movement keys, held/repeated/opposing input, release, Space reset, and focus loss.
- [Camera and window controls](camera-window.md): both interactive apps, camera reset, resize, hide/restore, Escape, and Close.
- [Public scene creation](scene-creation.md): scene descriptions, compilation, separate instances, shared geometry, and validation.
- [Headless simulation](headless-simulation.md): eight production ticks, zero-step preservation, split batches, and observations.
- [Offscreen rendering](offscreen-rendering.md): image output, exact coverage/depth, retained draws, and resource cleanup.
- [Textured materials](../../../../docs/textured-materials.md): vertex attributes, PNG cache release, sampling and lighting, camera updates, texture replacement and retention, shader controls, and the textured X11 example.

Application module registration is a developer API described in `docs/modules-registration.md`. This seed map does not claim exhaustive API coverage. Extend it when a task changes an unmapped user path.

# Entangle verification map

Read this index before choosing checks. Each file maps user actions to existing Bend drivers and observable results. The map describes coverage to run, not a claim that every path passed in the latest session.

## Baseline preconditions

- Run from the repository root with the toolchain and dependency revisions in `toolchain.bend`.
- Use the skill's fresh runtime and owned display for native window checks. Drivers find only their own child window.
- Run the doctor before input. Preserve evidence outside disposable runtime state.
- Run gates that write fixed repository `build` paths sequentially. Do not drive or terminate another session's app.
- Read `AGENTS.md`. Use formal laws, real runtime checks, and live input/replay evidence. Add no unit tests or mocks.

## Driving conventions

The executable `tools/verify-window-session.sh` launcher drives mesh movement. For additional camera-window scenarios, follow that feature recipe with its own owned display and runtime. CPU and offscreen recipes are independent shell invocations. They create their own evidence directory and exit after the real process returns.

For an optional window block, copy `tools/verify-window-session.sh` into the ignored `build/verification` directory, insert the block before its `run window ...` command, and run that copy from the repository root. Keep the copied script with the evidence. Do not edit the shared launcher or run the block after its display has been cleaned up.

Use the exact key symbols and native driver modes in the feature files. Do not infer desktop coverage from a headless run. Do not reuse archived captures as evidence for a new build.

## Proof and skip reporting

Record the feature ID, entry point, command, output, exit status, and resulting state. For UI changes, retain captures, native action/state traces where available, and zero-object shutdown logs. For file output, inspect the resulting file. Report build failures and missing display, validation layer, or device prerequisites explicitly.

A mesh pass covers the mesh entry of camera controls. It does not establish the cube entry. A creation CLI pass does not establish rendered colors or depth. If a change affects multiple entries, run all affected entries or list those skipped.

## Features

Use the [verification profiles](../../../../docs/development.md#run-verification) to select required checks. Profile success is scoped to its listed scenarios.

- [Formal laws](formal-laws.md): production Bend definitions, the universal upload-range theorem, mutation controls, and synchronization records.
- [S41 math qualification](../../../../docs/verification/2026-11-05-jonmath/README.md): explicit candidate adapters, numerical contracts, sensitivity controls, and exact retained scene comparisons through the `math` profile.
- [Source assets](../../../../docs/assets.md#verification-and-limits): typed cache handles, real file loading, cached failures, release/retry, exact retained mesh and material sources, source-only dependency closure, and scene execution after source release.
- [PNG source images](images.md): pinned decoder, retained real images, complete-pixel comparison, file/cache/retry behavior and production mutation controls.
- [Static OBJ sources](models.md): pinned parser, exact mesh/material/label conversion, file/cache/retry, source-only closure, real ECS/offscreen geometry, and owned X11 culling evidence.
- [JSON scene files and manifests](json-scene.md): one pinned parser, strict schema and reference validation, bounded loading, cache/retry, source preservation, and real ECS/offscreen evidence.
- [Checked host uploads](upload-boundary.md): enforced source policy, exact production payload lengths, real Vulkan writes and readback, rejection, and cleanup.
- [Mesh replacement](mesh-replacement.md): both renderer APIs, changed pixels and ranges, rejected-candidate preservation, recorded commands, multiple submissions, uniform and sampled-image descriptor retention, memory aliases, atomic retirement rejection, collection, and cleanup.
- [Native resource failures](resource-failures.md): recording/submission/reset rejection, real allocation failure under a process limit, partial preparation rollback, cleanup diagnostics, terminal teardown, and bounded proofs of production handlers for rare driver errors.
- [Mesh movement](mesh-movement.md): six movement keys, held/repeated/opposing input, release, Space reset, and focus loss.
- [Camera and window controls](camera-window.md): both interactive apps, camera reset, resize, hide/restore, Escape, and Close.

def measured(+dest:String,+label:String,+count:U32,+mode:U32,+repeat:U32) -> IO(String):

## E4 — Assets and a conventional 3D scene

**Goal:** the engine accepts prepared assets and creates an interactive scene.

### Tasks

- [x] Add a minimal Asset API: handles, loading/error state, a cache, and release rules. Landed on `main` as `513e5e4`: [API reference](docs/assets.md), [source](src/asset.bend), and [trail 23](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/23). Root lifecycle laws, real file loading/retry, and scene execution after source release pass. Scope names must be unique across handle lifetimes; native resource ownership is unchanged.

Other E4 tasks remain incomplete.

The typed loading boundary validates schema, F32 ranges, decoded-key uniqueness, asset references and size/depth/count limits. The [verification record](docs/verification/2026-11-04-json-scene/README.md) covers real files, cache/retry, exact ECS/offscreen output, frontend laws and sensitivity controls. - [x] Evaluate Jonlib math reuse through [explicit qualification adapters](docs/verification/2026-11-05-jonmath/README.md) for the current scene and mesh consumers [S41]. Retain Entangle's production math. Adapted multiplication and quaternion/TRS words match the checked inputs, while direct projection replacement violates Vulkan depth. Root arithmetic-contract laws, sensitivity controls, and exact retained ECS/geometry/RGBA/D32 comparisons pass. Current consumers need no geometric collision query. The completed evaluation and its publication state are tracked under [Trail 29](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/29).
- [x] Extend the position/color vertex format with UVs and normals. ### Importer and math limits

At the reviewed revision, Jonlib's standard PNG profile limits dimensions to 4096 per side and encoded input to 2 MiB. It supports variants, including Adam7 and 16-bit samples, beyond ezimg's PNG subset. Validate the selected profile with real assets and explicit rejection paths; a compiler check alone does not choose a decoder [S41, S43].

Jonmath's `Matrix.multiply(left, right)` computes `right × left` in column-vector notation. Entangle's matrix function computes `left × right`. Preserve the existing Vulkan projection and choose a fixed numerical contract instead of switching simulation results according to the host's libm profile [S41].

The [native S41 qualification](docs/verification/2026-11-05-jonmath/README.md) confirms that operand reversal and explicit field conversion preserve the checked multiplication and quaternion/TRS words. Production keeps its existing column layout, F32 operation order, quaternion validation, and Vulkan projection. No Jonmath numerical profile or collision API is introduced. The opt-in `math` workflow profile reproduces the decision and retained-scene comparisons.

Defer GLB until a consumer needs it. Jonlib's reviewed loader accepts a restricted binary glTF subset, rejects text `.gltf`, and truncates indices to 16 bits for raylib compatibility. An Entangle adapter must reject out-of-range indices before truncation or preserve U32 indices in a revised importer. Jonlib's software drawing and shader-uniform wrappers do not implement Entangle's textured Vulkan renderer or lighting [S41].

**Done when:** both applications use the public API, one scene loads from disk, loading errors do not break the application, and assets do not require manual Vulkan calls.

**Out of scope:** all of glTF, skeletal animation, PBR, an editor, hot reload, or a universal asset dependency graph.

command is a frontend proof check. Only the standalone upload command above
runs the BendTT kernel. Do not describe the root result as a kernel verdict.

`build/verification/law-mutations-*` directory. It checks unchanged sources,
changes one production definition at a time, restores each definition, and
checks the restored sources. It preserves laws and proofs throughout.

the expected `Location: Laws.<name>`. A parser error or timeout is not a
successful negative control. The driver records source hashes, changed
definitions, logs, and statuses. Retain the printed evidence directory.

exercise `geometry_install_reject`, `time_high_water`,

claim mutation coverage of every root law. Asset controls retain a released

+# Scene hierarchy
+
+The [contract](../../../../docs/scene-hierarchy.md) defines keep-local reparenting,
+`parent_global * T * R * S`, full affine globals, inverse-transpose normals,
+per-object world AABBs, and atomic rejection before publication. ECS owns mutable
+state; globals and world bounds are derived. E5 persistent RenderScene is separate.
+
+Run `verify-workflow --plan native hierarchy textured-window`, then those profiles.
+For a focused run use `hierarchy hierarchy-window`. The runner records exact source
+and per-stage status; incomplete stages never count as passes.
+
+`tools/hierarchy/runtime.bend` runs actual ECS flat forests, a 128-node chain,
+63-node branches, public edits, scheduled motion, reparent/detach, independent
+branches, and exact rejection preservation. Foreign namespace, stale generation,
+missing slot, self-link, cycle, singular lit ancestry, and non-finite transforms
+must fail. Real JSON files establish forward placement references and multipart
+anchors. The point/bounds oracle walks local transforms directly, without using
+production matrix multiplication. It checks relative error at `1e-4`.
+
+`render.bend` compares eight actual ECS states with independently baked geometry
+and tangent-derived normals through the actual offscreen renderer. Compare every
+RGBA byte within one UNORM step and D32 value within `2e-6`; require drawn coverage.
+`replay.bend` re-executes the captured public commands against the real application
+and compares complete handle, local, accepted, global, and bounds bit strings.
+`verify-hierarchy.bend` retains runtime traces and executes their replay.
+
+`mutations.bend` runs passing runtime/render baselines, then separately breaks
+cycle detection, parent composition, world bounds, publication, JSON parent
+expansion, and inverse-transpose normals. Require each named behavioral failure,
+then a passing restored build. Law controls separately break composition, cycle
+detection, bounds derivation, and rejection preservation.
+
+The owned Xwayland launcher supports `hierarchy` and includes hierarchy in
+`extended`. Keys 1–5 translate/rotate/scale/reparent/detach; R restores exact
+pixels. Keys 6–9 attempt invalid changes; the driver waits for the recorded
+acknowledgement before checking unchanged pixels. It checks resize/restore/Close,
+clean Vulkan validation, zero live objects, and replays the entire state trace.
+Inspect retained initial/moved/reset captures and cleanup records.
+
+`benchmark.bend` measures accepted root updates and full offscreen frames with
+readback. Final analytic forest state and every RGBA/D32 byte are recorded outside
+the timed interval. `measure.bend` alternates five baseline/candidate pairs for
+1000 flat nodes, 256 chain nodes, and 1023 branching nodes; identical complete state
+and image bytes are mandatory. The source receipt must identify both binaries.
+
+Root laws are frontend production-expression proofs, not a kernel theorem of
+floating-point accuracy or all forests. Runtime evidence covers the available
+Linux Vulkan lane. No spawn/despawn, keep-world reparenting, subtree bounds,
+incremental propagation, persistent RenderScene, or cross-backend claim is made.
