## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/home/aivv/.agents/skills`
- `r1` = `/home/aivv/.codex/skills/.system`
- `r2` = `/home/aivv/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/pages/0.1.26/skills`
- `r3` = `/home/aivv/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote`
- `r4` = `/home/aivv/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/sites/1.1.3/skills`
- `r5` = `/home/aivv/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/work-pets/0.1.6/skills`
- `r6` = `/home/aivv/Документы/projects/entangle/.agents/skills`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r1/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r1/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r1/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r1/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
- verify-entangle: Verify Entangle's source assets, PNG decoder, production laws, native rendering and resource behavior, and X11 controls/replay through existing drivers. Select affected checks after code or verification changes. (file: r6/verify-entangle/SKILL.md)
- verify-native-failures: Verify production Vulkan failure handlers after changes to native command recording, submission, device health, reset, completion, descriptor cleanup, or Entry.close. Use alongside verify-entangle for resource lifecycle changes. (file: r6/verify-native-failures/SKILL.md)
- architect: Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, 'architect this', 'design this', or an unresolved ownership, representation, or public API decision. Sketch directly by default. (file: r0/architect/SKILL.md)
- automate-me: Use for "automate me", "create/update/refresh my -mode skill", "turn/capture my preferences or working style into a skill", or wanting agents to follow how the user works. Drafts or revises a personal -mode skill via the authoring-a-skill playbook, optionally pulling fresh evidence from recent threads. (file: r0/automate-me/SKILL.md)
- benchmark-checklist: Vet a perf measurement (limiter, tuning, limits, errors, repeatability, relevance, and whether the work happened) before you report or act on it. Use when you run a benchmark or report a speedup or regression you measured. (file: r0/benchmark-checklist/SKILL.md)
- blast-radius: Find what a change could break somewhere else before it ships, beyond the diff, and prove the one fact it's safe because of by running real code instead of writing it up. Use for 'blast radius of X', 'what could this break', or reviewing a small diff you don't trust. (file: r0/blast-radius/SKILL.md)
- bro: Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon. (file: r0/bro/SKILL.md)
- correct: Find the mistakes agents keep repeating in this repo and make each one impossible. Try architecture first, then types, then a lint whose error names the fix, then a test, and write docs last. Prove each check fails on a real past mistake. Repeat this each time the operator corrects you. Use for /correct. (file: r0/correct/SKILL.md)
- create-formal-verification-skill: Generate a project-local skill that formally verifies the code where a bug costs the most and tests reach the least, in any language, with whichever verification tool fits. Use for /create-formal-verification-skill, "model-check this race", "prove this invariant", or when concurrency, retries, state machines, parsers, or unsafe code need more than tests. (file: r0/create-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md)
- create-verification-skill: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives your app the way a user does — any language, framework, or platform. Use for /create-verification-skill, "make a control skill for this repo", or when a project has no scripted way to prove UI/CLI/service behavior. (file: r0/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md)
- figure-it-out: Design an auditable playbook when no narrower one fits: a large migration, an ambitious multi-part change, or work a human reviews after stepping away. Scales rigor to the task, runs a hypothesis loop, and logs decisions. Use for /figure-it-out or 'figure it out'. (file: r0/figure-it-out/SKILL.md)
- how: Use for "how does X work", code walkthroughs before changing something, and placement / ownership / layering questions ("where should this live", "which package owns this", "is this the right layer"). Explains subsystem architecture, runtime flow, onboarding mental models. Use why for motivation. (file: r0/how/SKILL.md)
- in-your-own-words: Restate in your own words what you think the user's goals are and what problem they're trying to solve. Use for /in-your-own-words. (file: r0/in-your-own-words/SKILL.md)
- ketchup: Catch the user up on what changed in this chat since their last message, in plain words and small visuals. List every item waiting on them with what they need to decide it from the reply alone. Use for /ketchup. (file: r0/ketchup/SKILL.md)
- ketchup-video: Catch the user up like /ketchup, with a short subtitled video of slides for what happened and the waiting calls as text under it. Use for /ketchup-video. (file: r0/ketchup-video/SKILL.md)
- maintain-formal-verification-skill: Bring a project's formal verification back in line with the code after the code changes: find the commits that touched verified code, update the model, harness, or properties to describe the code as it is now, rerun, and say whether each failure is drift in the verification or a bug in the code. Use for /maintain-formal-verification-skill, "is the model still true to the code", or after merges and refactors that touched verified code without rechecking it. (file: r0/maintain-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md)
- maintain-verification-skill: Periodic pass that keeps a project's verification skill and feature map honest: parallel source readers per feature, one live session driving every feature, at most one PR of proven corrections. Use for /maintain-verification-skill or "audit the verify skill". (file: r0/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md)
- make-bot-ui: Use when building a custom UI (page, dashboard, buttons) that should wake the agent over a webhook, when the user must provide a webhook secret, or when exposing that UI on Tailscale. (file: r0/make-bot-ui/SKILL.md)
- p3-help: Guides users through p3-stack setup, /p3-mode, and picking the skill, playbook, or principle for a task. Use for /p3-help, or when the user asks how to install, set up, or use p3-stack, or which p3-stack skill fits. Not for requests to do work, even ones that name p3-stack. (file: r0/p3-help/SKILL.md)
- p3-mode: p3 agent style for concise, detailed responses, deliberate delegation, clear prose, simple code, and verified work. Use for p3, /p3-mode, or requests to work in this style. (file: r0/p3-mode/SKILL.md)
- pages:maintain-space: Reconcile new evidence into existing ChatGPT Pages or a Space when the user requests upkeep. For a direct text correction, use write-page. Do not use for ordinary chat drafts, writing, or advice, or treat a selected Page as a request to save. Schedule future upkeep only when requested. (file: r2/maintain-space/SKILL.md)
- pages:manage-schedules: Review a ChatGPT Space page and its schedules, recommend useful recurring work, and create, update, or remove scheduled automations. (file: r2/manage-schedules/SKILL.md)
- pages:organize-space: Organize existing ChatGPT Pages and Space structure when the user requests changes to that structure. Do not use for ordinary chat drafts or advice; a selected Page alone does not authorize reorganization. A narrow text edit does not need this workflow. (file: r2/organize-space/SKILL.md)
- pages:write-page: Create or edit requested Page/Space content, or use for prose you have already decided to save as a standalone Markdown file, only if the user did not explicitly request a Markdown file. Honor established formats, destinations, and repository documentation. A selected Page alone does not authorize a write. (file: r2/write-page/SKILL.md)
- plugin-management:plugin-management: Discover and suggest relevant plugins, inspect app permissions and dependencies, and manage plugin connections or removal. Use when the user asks about plugins or when a task would materially benefit from an external app, account, service, or data source that available tools cannot access. (file: r3/plugin-management/0.1.0/skills/plugin-management/SKILL.md)
- principle-attack-the-premise: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it. (file: r0/principle-attack-the-premise/SKILL.md)
- principle-boundary-discipline: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions. (file: r0/principle-boundary-discipline/SKILL.md)
- principle-build-the-lever: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun. (file: r0/principle-build-the-lever/SKILL.md)
- principle-encode-lessons-in-structure: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text. (file: r0/principle-encode-lessons-in-structure/SKILL.md)
- principle-exhaust-the-design-space: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing. (file: r0/principle-exhaust-the-design-space/SKILL.md)
- principle-experience-first: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones. (file: r0/principle-experience-first/SKILL.md)
- principle-explain-the-number: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think. (file: r0/principle-explain-the-number/SKILL.md)
- principle-fix-root-causes: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate. (file: r0/principle-fix-root-causes/SKILL.md)
- principle-foundational-thinking: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious. (file: r0/principle-foundational-thinking/SKILL.md)
- principle-guard-the-context-window: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads. (file: r0/principle-guard-the-context-window/SKILL.md)
- principle-laziness-protocol: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem. (file: r0/principle-laziness-protocol/SKILL.md)
- principle-make-operations-idempotent: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs. (file: r0/principle-make-operations-idempotent/SKILL.md)
- principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers. (file: r0/principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis/SKILL.md)
- principle-minimize-reader-load: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope. (file: r0/principle-minimize-reader-load/SKILL.md)
- principle-model-the-domain: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. (file: r0/principle-model-the-domain/SKILL.md)
- principle-never-block-on-the-human: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work. (file: r0/principle-never-block-on-the-human/SKILL.md)
- principle-outcome-oriented-execution: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code. (file: r0/principle-outcome-oriented-execution/SKILL.md)
- principle-prove-it-works: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.' (file: r0/principle-prove-it-works/SKILL.md)
- principle-redesign-from-first-principles: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. (file: r0/principle-redesign-from-first-principles/SKILL.md)
- principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant. (file: r0/principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state/SKILL.md)
- principle-sequence-verifiable-units: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer. (file: r0/principle-sequence-verifiable-units/SKILL.md)
- principle-subtract-before-you-add: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base. (file: r0/principle-subtract-before-you-add/SKILL.md)
- principle-test-behavior-not-implementation: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so that the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change. (file: r0/principle-test-behavior-not-implementation/SKILL.md)
- principle-type-system-discipline: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas. (file: r0/principle-type-system-discipline/SKILL.md)
- recall: Reconstruct your recent working context from your own chat history, live state, and the shared record (user reports, prior fixes, incidents), then hand back a tight current-state brief. Use for 'recall my work on X', 'catch me up', 'what have I been working on', 'where did I leave off', before starting or resuming work. (file: r0/recall/SKILL.md)
- reflect: Spawn three parallel review subagents over the active transcript, surface learnings, and route each to a concrete edit on an existing skill. Use when the user says reflect. (file: r0/reflect/SKILL.md)
- setup-p3: Configure which models p3-stack uses per role and at what reasoning budget. Detects your available models and writes p3-models.md, which overrides the skill defaults. Use for /setup-p3, "configure p3 models", "p3 budget", or changing p3-stack's model choices. (file: r0/setup-p3/SKILL.md)
- sharpen: Make a task deeper, not bigger, then rewrite the prompt. Use for /sharpen. (file: r0/sharpen/SKILL.md)
- show-me-your-work: Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result). <t3_code_orchestration_01>## T3 Code orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no T3 tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers, and no settings beyond yours (Claude `Agent`, `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Use `delegate_task` for another provider's model, user-asked settings, a separate checkout (`isolation:"worktree"`), or `delegate_task` by name. A native type on another provider's model counts too. Background agent: `delegate_task`, never a background `Agent`. Workflow only when asked.
- Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once per thread, before the first `delegate_task`. Again only after an error or a user-named provider change. Settings go in `target.options`. Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked, or fall back to native tools, Workflow, or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.
- Every new delegate review or re-check is a new `delegate_task` (brief, findings, objections), never a `t3_thread_send`. Fix small review findings yourself; start no delegate for them. When told to proceed without a delegate, or to run fewer, `task_cancel` the extras. Start no replacement.
- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Do not poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `t3_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- If you are a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.</t3_code_orchestration_01>

<t3_code_orchestration_02>- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`; shell worktrees do not bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `t3_thread_read` it before you answer about it.
- Another machine: `t3_environment_links` lists linked ones. Pass its `environmentId` to a T3 tool to act there. Ids are then that machine's, so pass `threadId`.
- A machine the user names that is not linked ("delegate this to my vps"): call `t3_environment_link` with a `hint` from their words. Never ask for a pairing code in chat.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim. Never a plain title or bare id.
- A login, token, PIN or pairing code only the user can give: call `request_secret`, not a chat ask or a handoff. Not for access you have. When asked only to schedule, `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.</t3_code_orchestration_02>

<t3_code_orchestration_03>### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart, and show any visual the user asks for here: pass its HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. If the visual is a file, pass that file's HTML. A screenshot on disk or a text description does not show it. Never start a server for it. Tools a web page exposes give data only. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send, or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` unasked to verify or show your own edit. Use them when the current request asks for browser work, including recording edits, or names a page or tab. Do not repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.</t3_code_orchestration_03>

<t3_code_runtime><runtime_info>In case you're asked: you are running in T3 Code through the Codex harness, as gpt-6-astra with xhigh reasoning effort. No need to mention this otherwise. You can embed images, video, and audio in your response using Markdown image syntax with absolute file paths. Link any other file you produce using its absolute path so the user can open it in T3 Code's files viewer.</runtime_info>

<pull_request_linking>
Link each PR you create, take over, or push to: link_pull_request, or link_pull_requests for several, full URL, every stack layer, as your next call. Host tools do not link for you. If linking fails, say so. Skip PRs you only read or review, and PRs named only as background. Call watch_pull_request when asked to monitor or babysit, or when work you were asked to do, such as a merge, still waits on checks or reviews, even after an earlier unwatch. Finish any needed branch update and push first, then watch and end your turn. Otherwise act now or hand back. Delegated children never watch, even if the brief says babysit. After PR work, a child's last line is: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>. Links and watches persist across pushes. For PR waits, no sleep, loops, gh --watch, Monitor or ScheduleWakeup. Before handback, call unwatch_pull_request on any PR you watch.
</pull_request_linking></t3_code_runtime>

<t3_code_tools>

## T3 Code browser

When browser work was asked, `preview_*` is the browser you share with the user: `preview_status` first, then `preview_open` if no tab can be automated. Prefer snapshot locators over coordinates. Switch browsers only if the tools are absent or `preview_open` says unsupported, the user asks, or two preview calls fail on one step. Then quote the error and switch.
</t3_code_tools>

# E4 scene hierarchy: November 5, 2026

Task: [Trail 31](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/31).
Implementation is local on top of `dc70d54`. No commit, publication, or merge is
claimed. The [contract](../../scene-hierarchy.md) records the semantics and
acceptance criteria established before implementation.

## Implemented

Creation descriptions and version 1 JSON accept optional parents, including
forward references. JSON placement references are translated to model-part
anchors. The real ECS owns local transforms, relationships, source bounds, and
rollback checkpoints. Full sequential derivation publishes complete affine
globals and per-object world AABBs. Public edits reject invalid graphs, handles,
and numerical state before writing; scheduled invalid spatial results restore
accepted locals. Both renderers consume the resulting world transforms.
Inverse-transpose normal matrices preserve lighting with nonuniform ancestor
scale, rotation, and shear. Flat root draws retain their representation.

## Verification status

Final source-specific workflow receipt is pending. Preliminary actual ECS,
independent geometry/lighting readbacks, deterministic replay, frontend laws,
and all six runtime sensitivity controls passed. Final status will be recorded
here after the required profiles complete; this paragraph is not a final pass.

The new checks execute production ECS and Vulkan paths. The numerical oracle
walks local transforms directly rather than using production matrix composition.
The lighting oracle builds normals from transformed tangents. Render comparison
covers complete RGBA/D32 output, with one UNORM step and `2e-6` depth tolerance.
Replay compares complete local/accepted/global/bounds and entity identity bits.
Root laws quantify production expressions; they are frontend checks, not a
kernel theorem of arbitrary graph or floating-point correctness. The existing
standalone upload kernel verdict remains a separate check.

## Constrained performance evaluation

One performance change was attempted and retained provisionally pending the
final correctness receipt. No parallel or incremental evaluator was introduced.

The initial 1000-node phase probe measured about 485 ms reading ECS components,
0.92 ms deriving the forest, and 28.6 ms committing it. These were diagnostic
measurements under concurrent build load, not the comparison results below.
Inspection located repeated reconstruction of live handles in the per-component
inspector path. The hypothesis was that one captured ECS scope, retaining checked
namespace/generation access, would eliminate that repeated work. The declared
targets were publication time down at least 50% and end-to-end offscreen time down
at least 30%.

The comparison used five alternating pairs (order reversed each pair), six
accepted root updates per timing interval, one warm update/frame, native Bend
with one CPU thread and Bend GPU dispatch off, and an actual 256×256 Vulkan render and
readback per frame. Creation and output validation are outside the measured
interval. Every pair had identical complete ECS state and RGBA/D32 bytes.
Counters require all requested updates, valid analytic forest state, drawn
coverage, and zero live Vulkan objects after the scope.
The workloads use shared unlit quad geometry: a flat grid, a deep chain, and
a binary tree. Root translation alternates between two values. These timings
measure hierarchy publication and its rendering consumer, not asset loading,
complex-material throughput, or a presented window's frame rate.

Machine: AMD Ryzen 5 1600, 12 logical CPUs, GTX 1660, NVIDIA 615.78.08,
Linux x86-64, Bend 2.0.39, Clang 23.1.4. Ordinary desktop/browser processes were
active. The final-source repeat also overlapped a verification build; alternating
order gives both versions exposure to that load. An earlier run without a
concurrent compiler gave the same verdict. These are
wall-clock results for this machine, not a throughput limit or real-time promise.
The offscreen numbers include extraction, draw recording, rendering, and readback.

Values are median milliseconds per update/frame, with the range of five runs.

| Workload | Measurement | Baseline ms (range) | Captured read ms (range) | Reduction |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Flat 1000 | publication | 513.17 (493.06–531.65) | 65.85 (64.83–72.62) | 87.2% |
| Flat 1000 | offscreen-frame | 1010.44 (987.87–1044.26) | 188.50 (185.78–194.93) | 81.3% |
| Chain 256 | publication | 32.22 (31.58–32.55) | 5.96 (5.90–6.24) | 81.5% |
| Chain 256 | offscreen-frame | 149.47 (148.59–151.23) | 101.03 (100.07–103.65) | 32.4% |
| Branches 1023 | publication | 527.11 (518.49–547.10) | 70.47 (67.80–72.96) | 86.6% |
| Branches 1023 | offscreen-frame | 1035.19 (1033.14–1070.14) | 192.64 (188.52–194.49) | 81.4% |

The flat 1000-node workload set the target. The chain and branching workloads
were additional validation scenes. All met both targets; no second or third
performance change was attempted. Even the improved ~66 ms publication at 1000
nodes is unsuitable for a 60 Hz update budget. Checked membership/commit and
full-scene work remain costs for future measurement. E5 remains separate.

These results include the final textured-root detachment admission guard,
rejection scenarios, and migrated consumer extraction. The full source-specific correctness workflow
remains required. The [raw timings](performance.log), [source hashes](performance-sources.sha256),
[machine record](performance-machine.txt), and [chart](performance.html) are retained.

## Retained evidence and reproduction

Original evidence remains under `build/verification`:

- `hierarchy/`: decision trail, early runtime/render/replay logs, phase probe,
  comparison output, and build diagnostics.
- `hierarchy-controls-EPWHKwxX/`: passing baseline, six named production-source
  regressions, and six restored passing baselines.
- `hierarchy-measure-RUOmhiH9/`: all 30 comparison runs, exact state and image
  output, binary/source hashes, and machine information.
- `hierarchy-measure-5p2B0oeK/`: final-source repeat of all 30 runs, copied
  baseline/candidate executables, source hashes, full state/image comparisons,
  and machine/load information, before the last consumer migration.
- `hierarchy-measure-u8uQ1E0f/`: repeat after the consumer migration, with all 30
  runs' state/image outputs and both executables retained. This is the source
  of the table above. Baseline and candidate production sources differ only in
  the checked read path in `scene-hierarchy.bend`.
- `hierarchy-baseline-source/`: isolated baseline source and executable.

Run the registered workflow from the repository root:

```sh
bend tools/verify-workflow.bend -o build/verify-workflow
./build/verify-workflow --plan native hierarchy textured-window
./build/verify-workflow native hierarchy textured-window +RTS --threads 1 --gpu off
```

The focused profiles are `hierarchy hierarchy-window`. The
[feature map](../../../.agents/skills/verify-entangle/features/scene-hierarchy.md)
lists driver coverage and sensitivity expectations.

## Failed attempts and limits

Two early X11 attempts failed because the fixture used an offscreen camera with
window back-face culling, then because its supposed red texel was yellow. A third
standalone build encountered a temporary source parse error while the worktree
was being edited. Their evidence and cleanup records remain in
`entangle-z0JZWcAV`, `entangle-pZqHfv3U`, and `entangle-5PZIpxQ7`.
None is counted as a pass. Final workflow execution uses an isolated snapshot.

`entangle-LSokbavf` passed the hierarchy window and its 23-command replay, and the
mesh live scenario and 1427-batch replay. Hidden Close itself passed, but its trace
contained fewer than the replay gate's required 11 completed batches. The driver
now waits for recorded batches before closing. `workflow-CFQRV3cA` stopped at
source policy because the new JSON Null constructor and checked ECS access
symbols were absent from the reviewed inventory. The inventory now lists those
exact symbols. These failed receipts remain evidence of the corrected workflow,
not complete passes.

`workflow-aZeP21qn` was explicitly stopped and superseded after a consumer audit
found local-only draw construction in the mesh and textured examples. Both now
use the shared derived draw path, as do Creation/OBJ/JSON consumer snapshots.
Two extraction laws and a static-consumer sensitivity control were added before
the fresh `workflow-a8yf31nk` run. The superseded receipt is not a complete pass.

This scope excludes runtime spawn/despawn, preserve-world reparenting, subtree
bounds, runtime mesh/material rebinding, incremental propagation, persistent RenderScene, collision/culling use
of bounds, and CUDA/Metal/WebGPU execution claims. Negative scale preserves
affine semantics; existing window face-culling policy still applies. Numerical
normal-matrix limits are explicit admission constraints, not a proof of good
conditioning for all inputs. Resource lifetime algorithms and dependency pins
are unchanged.

# Develop and verify Entangle

Keep one owner for coupled production code, laws, and verification. Ordinary features and refactors do not require architect, arena, or adversarial-review panels. Delegate a bounded independent probe only when it answers a named uncertainty. Model-role configuration does not require a panel.

## Before implementation

In the existing task or Trail, record the observable outcome, the production functions that enforce it, the required checks, and their limits. Qualify an unfamiliar dependency with a small real input and an independently known output before designing the adapter. Keep that probe and its pinned dependency revision.

Use real files and native consumers for effects. Prove important general properties against production definitions. For rare driver results that cannot reliably be induced by valid runtime inputs, state the symbolic boundary and bounded proof scope in advance. Preserve the distinction between Bend frontend checks, kernel verdicts, bounded CBMC proofs, and observed hardware behavior.

A new or changed critical verifier needs a sensitivity control. The original implementation passes, a deliberate production-source regression violates the named property, and restored sources pass. A timeout, compiler crash, parse error, or unrelated rejection does not establish sensitivity. Fix the verifier when its oracle is wrong; do not weaken the production contract to make it green.

## Run verification

Run from the repository root. Build the runner natively so large evidence manifests do not depend on the interpreter stack.

```sh
bend guide
mkdir -p build
bend tools/verify-workflow.bend -o build/verify-workflow
./build/verify-workflow --plan assets images
./build/verify-workflow assets images +RTS --threads 1 --gpu off
```

`--plan` lists the selected stages and literal arguments without executing checks. Unknown or empty profile selections fail. Repeated profiles do not repeat stages. All selected stages are required. Source-policy checks run before product profiles, and real-runtime checks precede the expensive proof and mutation stages. Execution stops at the first failure; remaining stages stay `not_run`.

| Profile | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `toolchain` | Pinned Bend, Clang, target, platform, and clean dependency revisions. This alone is not product verification. |
| `proofs` | Root frontend proofs, standalone upload kernel verdict, law mutations and restored baselines. |
| `assets` | Root frontend proofs, law mutations, real file/cache/release/retry and source-consumer checks. |
| `images` | Assets plus PNG corpus, full-pixel comparison, real file/cache behavior and decoder mutations. |
| `json` | Assets plus strict scene/manifest files, reference and resource limits, cache/retry, parser qualification, production mutations and real ECS/offscreen comparison. |
| `math` | Pinned S41 adapter qualification, exact numerical contracts, production projection and adapter controls, root law mutations, and retained native scene/state/readback comparisons. Downloads the rejected candidate for evaluation only. |
| `textures` | Source laws, shader regeneration, real RGBA/D32 sampling and lighting, camera updates, texture rollback/retention/replacement, production mutations, and the native failure profile. |
| `hierarchy` | Root frontend laws and mutations, actual ECS forest/edit/rollback checks, JSON anchors, full-state replay, independent geometry/lighting readbacks, and seven production sensitivity controls. |
| `hierarchy-window` | Owned Xwayland hierarchy edits, pixel reset, rejection, resize/restore/Close, complete-state replay, plus mesh controls/replay. |
| `upload` | Root frontend proofs, upload kernel verdict, law and source-policy mutations, real production/native upload boundaries and readback. |
| `native-failures` | Root frontend proofs and law mutations, bounded production-handler proofs with all mutations, real resource failure/rollback/retry. |
| `native` | Existing default native/offscreen gate, plus kernel verdict and law, source-policy, and native-handler sensitivity controls. |
| `window` | Owned Xwayland mesh controls, focus/resize/Close, captures and full-state replay. Requires the parent Wayland session and validation layer. |
| `textured-window` | Owned Xwayland mesh, cube, creation, replacement, textured, and hierarchy windows. Includes camera controls, resize, restore, cleanup, and full-state replay. |
| `all` | `native` and the extended window scenarios. This covers the registered profiles, not every feature-map scenario or backend. |

No arguments selects `native`. Profiles combine by union. Run affected profiles during implementation and include their dependent consumers before completion. Use the [feature map](../.agents/skills/verify-entangle/features/README.md) for other scenarios, including cube/public-creation windows and replacement windows. Add a required scenario when a change introduces a new behavior; do not treat the current profile list as exhaustive. The merged OBJ importer is covered by `verify-models` within the default native gate. Its supported profile and additional X11 evidence are recorded in the feature map; there is no separate `models` profile.

The runner preserves a source snapshot under a fresh `build/verification/workflow-XXXXXXXX/source` directory. It copies current uncommitted sources, creates independent Git repositories for the root and pinned dependencies, checks source fingerprints before and after copying, and executes sequentially inside the snapshot. This supports both ordinary clones and Git worktrees; snapshot Git commands resolve to the copied files. Fixed legacy build paths and mutation copies stay there. It does not switch branches, overwrite another session's binaries, publish code, or remove evidence. Source changes during copying fail the run. Changes after copying do not invalidate the snapshot result, but that result does not certify the new working tree. The snapshot includes other uncommitted work already present in the source directories. Start from a task-specific checkout when that work must be excluded; snapshotting isolates execution, not the choice of patch.

The existing Bash launcher in `tools/verify-window-session.sh` retains the owned-process and signal-cleanup lifecycle from the skill. The Bend runner invokes it inside the snapshot. A standalone launcher invocation retains its own evidence directory. Other shell recipes in the feature map are additional scenarios, not implicit coverage of this launcher.

## Read the result

`manifest.tsv` records the required stage, evidence kind, argv file, stdout, stderr, and status file. Each `.argv` file contains one literal argument per line, starting with the executable. Each stage status starts as `not_run`, becomes `running`, then records its exit code or `process_error:<code>`. Logs remain separate even on failure.

A complete pass requires `state` to be `complete`, `run.status` to be zero, and every manifest stage status to be zero. A missing, interrupted, failed, or unexecuted required stage is not a pass. `run.status` starts nonzero so setup errors and interruption cannot leave a successful receipt. Inspect the actual driver output and relevant captures as prescribed by the feature map.

The receipt includes the root revision, dirty diff and status, dependency revisions, compiler/platform details, source fingerprints, requested profiles, and timestamps. Full untracked source content is retained in the snapshot. Nested drivers retain their own detailed evidence under its `build/verification` directory. Keep the snapshot while its result is used; do not reuse a receipt for changed sources, harnesses, tools, dependencies, or relevant environment.

## Complete the task

Update code, applicable laws, sensitivity controls, coverage and task state together. Link the receipt and state its limits. Re-run only checks invalidated by a relevant edit or unresolved failure; do not add a generic review panel after acceptance passes.

Refresh the roadmap's current summary, next action, and affected checklist. Read live Entire change state before reporting publication or merge. Record implementation completion, task closure, and merged code separately. Preserve historical evidence at its original revision. Publishing and merging remain subject to the user's existing authorization.

The [workflow verification record](verification/2026-11-04-development-workflow/README.md) records the rollout, failure controls, and scoped full run.

# Scene hierarchy

The [contract](../../../../docs/scene-hierarchy.md) defines keep-local reparenting,
`parent_global * T * R * S`, full affine globals, inverse-transpose normals,
per-object world AABBs, and atomic rejection before publication. ECS owns mutable
state; globals and world bounds are derived. E5 persistent RenderScene is separate.

Run `verify-workflow --plan native hierarchy textured-window`, then those profiles.
For a focused run use `hierarchy hierarchy-window`. The runner records exact source
and per-stage status; incomplete stages never count as passes.

`tools/hierarchy/runtime.bend` runs actual ECS flat forests, a 128-node chain,
63-node branches, public edits, scheduled motion, reparent/detach, independent
branches, and exact rejection preservation. Foreign namespace, stale generation,
missing slot, self-link, cycle, singular lit ancestry, and non-finite transforms
must fail. Real JSON files establish forward placement references and multipart
anchors. The point/bounds oracle walks local transforms directly, without using
production matrix multiplication. It checks relative error at `1e-4`.

`render.bend` compares eight actual ECS states with independently baked geometry
and tangent-derived normals through the actual offscreen renderer. Compare every
RGBA byte within one UNORM step and D32 value within `2e-6`; require drawn coverage.
`replay.bend` re-executes the captured public commands against the real application
and compares complete handle, local, accepted, global, and bounds bit strings.
`verify-hierarchy.bend` retains runtime traces and executes their replay.

`mutations.bend` runs passing runtime/render baselines, then separately breaks
cycle detection, parent composition, world bounds, publication, JSON parent
expansion, inverse-transpose normals, and static consumer extraction. Require each
named behavioral failure, then a passing restored build. Law controls separately
break composition, cycle detection, bounds derivation, rejection preservation,
and child draw extraction. Static textured seed draws must match the complete
derived draw values of the actual ECS. The mesh application and Creation/OBJ/JSON
consumers use the same public derived extraction path.

The owned Xwayland launcher supports `hierarchy` and includes hierarchy in
`extended`. Keys 1–5 translate/rotate/scale/reparent/detach; R restores exact
pixels. Keys 6–9 attempt invalid changes; the driver waits for the recorded
acknowledgement before checking unchanged pixels. It checks resize/restore/Close,
clean Vulkan validation, zero live objects, and replays the entire state trace.
Inspect retained initial/moved/reset captures and cleanup records.

`benchmark.bend` measures accepted root updates and full offscreen frames with
readback. Final analytic forest state and every RGBA/D32 byte are recorded outside
the timed interval. `measure.bend` alternates five baseline/candidate pairs for
1000 flat nodes, 256 chain nodes, and 1023 branching nodes; identical complete state
and image bytes are mandatory. The source receipt must identify both binaries.

Root laws are frontend production-expression proofs, not a kernel theorem of
floating-point accuracy or all forests. Runtime evidence covers the available
Linux Vulkan lane. No spawn/despawn, keep-world reparenting, subtree bounds,
incremental propagation, persistent RenderScene, or cross-backend claim is made.

### Tasks

- [x] Add a minimal Asset API: handles, loading/error state, a cache, and release rules. Landed on `main` as `513e5e4`: [API reference](docs/assets.md), [source](src/asset.bend), and [trail 23](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/23). Root lifecycle laws, real file loading/retry, and scene execution after source release pass. Scope names must be unique across handle lifetimes; native resource ownership is unchanged.
- [x] Define an [internal mesh and material format](docs/content.md) independent of the importer.
- [x] Select and integrate one [PNG image decoder](docs/image-decoder.md). Native comparison of pinned Jonlib and `emerging-ezimg` on retained cat photos, PNG variants, and engine captures qualifies Jonlib [S41, S43]. Accepted variants, limits, layout, errors, licenses, and reproduction are recorded in the [verification evidence](docs/verification/2026-11-04-image-decoder/README.md). QOI is not added.
- [x] Start the [static-model importer](docs/model-obj.md) with validated Jonlib S41 `src/obj.bend`. Ordered mesh/material/label sources load synchronously through Assets without ECS or Vulkan ownership. The authored-triangle/diffuse profile, exact pin/licenses, properties, file/cache behavior, and real imported Creation/ECS/offscreen/X11 evidence are [recorded](docs/verification/2026-11-04-model-obj/README.md). Other E4 tasks remain incomplete.
- [x] Select `bend-kit-json@0.7.0.0` for [JSON scene files and manifests](docs/json-scene.md) [S44]. The typed loading boundary validates schema, F32 ranges, decoded-key uniqueness, asset references and size/depth/count limits. The [verification record](docs/verification/2026-11-04-json-scene/README.md) covers real files, cache/retry, exact ECS/offscreen output, frontend laws and sensitivity controls. Present on local and remote `main` at `ac805c7`, as checked during the S41 evaluation. The original evidence retains its historical local implementation state under [Trail 28](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/28).
- [x] Evaluate Jonlib math reuse through [explicit qualification adapters](docs/verification/2026-11-05-jonmath/README.md) for the current scene and mesh consumers [S41]. Retain Entangle's production math. Adapted multiplication and quaternion/TRS words match the checked inputs, while direct projection replacement violates Vulkan depth. Root arithmetic-contract laws, sensitivity controls, and exact retained ECS/geometry/RGBA/D32 comparisons pass. Current consumers need no geometric collision query. The completed evaluation and its publication state are tracked under [Trail 29](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/29).
- [x] Extend the position/color vertex format with UVs and normals. [Textured materials and directional lighting](docs/textured-materials.md) now use real RGBA8 upload, deferred texture ownership, the existing camera, and both Vulkan rendering paths [S53]. The [textured cube example](examples/textured-scene.bend) loads a PNG through Assets. Implementation and verification are complete; [Trail 30](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/30) records publication state.
- [ ] Add scene descriptions, a Transform → GlobalTransform hierarchy, and rejection of parent cycles.
- [ ] Correctly update dependent transforms/bounds when a parent changes; this must feed into future render change tracking.
- [ ] Check corrupted files, missing assets, unsupported variants, and repeated loading.
- [ ] Make a model viewer and a small scene with gameplay interaction the two required consumers.

### Importer and math limits

At the reviewed revision, Jonlib's standard PNG profile limits dimensions to 4096 per side and encoded input to 2 MiB. It supports variants, including Adam7 and 16-bit samples, beyond ezimg's PNG subset. Validate the selected profile with real assets and explicit rejection paths; a compiler check alone does not choose a decoder [S41, S43].

Jonmath's `Matrix.multiply(left, right)` computes `right × left` in column-vector notation. Entangle's matrix function computes `left × right`. Preserve the existing Vulkan projection and choose a fixed numerical contract instead of switching simulation results according to the host's libm profile [S41].

The [native S41 qualification](docs/verification/2026-11-05-jonmath/README.md) confirms that operand reversal and explicit field conversion preserve the checked multiplication and quaternion/TRS words. Production keeps its existing column layout, F32 operation order, quaternion validation, and Vulkan projection. No Jonmath numerical profile or collision API is introduced. The opt-in `math` workflow profile reproduces the decision and retained-scene comparisons.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Append a well-formed row to a show-me-your-work decision log (TSV).
# Usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>
set -euo pipefail

if [ "$#" -ne 6 ]; then
	printf 'usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\n' >&2
	exit 1
fi

logfile="$1"
shift

logdir="$(dirname "$logfile")"
if [ -n "$logdir" ] && [ "$logdir" != "." ] && [ ! -d "$logdir" ]; then
	mkdir -p "$logdir"
fi

# Use `>>` here, never `>`. A network mount can fail this test for a log
# that exists. Then the cost is one stray header line, not the rows.
if [ ! -s "$logfile" ]; then
	printf 'ts\tphase\tdecision\twhy\tevidence\tresult\n' >> "$logfile"
fi

ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
# Strip tabs/newlines/CR so cells stay on one line, and prefix any cell
# whose first char a spreadsheet would parse as a formula (=, +, -, @)
# with a single quote. The skill expects this log to be read in
# spreadsheets, so attacker-controlled evidence (PR titles, filenames,
# generated text) must not become formula execution when a reviewer
# opens the file.
clean() {
	local v
	v=$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '\t\n\r' '   ')
	case "$v" in
		=*|+*|-*|@*) printf "'%s" "$v" ;;
		*) printf '%s' "$v" ;;

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Append a well-formed row to a show-me-your-work decision log (TSV).
# Usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>
set -euo pipefail

if [ "$#" -ne 6 ]; then
	printf 'usage: log.sh <logfile> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>\n' >&2
	exit 1
fi

logfile="$1"
shift

logdir="$(dirname "$logfile")"
if [ -n "$logdir" ] && [ "$logdir" != "." ] && [ ! -d "$logdir" ]; then
	mkdir -p "$logdir"
fi

# Use `>>` here, never `>`. A network mount can fail this test for a log
# that exists. Then the cost is one stray header line, not the rows.
if [ ! -s "$logfile" ]; then
	printf 'ts\tphase\tdecision\twhy\tevidence\tresult\n' >> "$logfile"
fi

ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
# Strip tabs/newlines/CR so cells stay on one line, and prefix any cell
# whose first char a spreadsheet would parse as a formula (=, +, -, @)
# with a single quote. The skill expects this log to be read in
# spreadsheets, so attacker-controlled evidence (PR titles, filenames,
# generated text) must not become formula execution when a reviewer
# opens the file.
clean() {
	local v
	v=$(printf '%s' "$1" | tr '\t\n\r' '   ')
	case "$v" in
		=*|+*|-*|@*) printf "'%s" "$v" ;;
		*) printf '%s' "$v" ;;
	esac
}
printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
	"$ts" "$(clean "$1")" "$(clean "$2")" "$(clean "$3")" "$(clean "$4")" "$(clean "$5")" \
	>> "$logfile"
"}

# Scene hierarchy

Implementation task: [Trail 31](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/31).
The semantics and acceptance below were recorded before implementation.

## Semantics and ownership

Each scene instance has one optional parent, identified by its zero-based source
instance index. Forward references are allowed. Roots have no parent. The graph
must be a forest. Self-parenting, cycles, and missing parents are errors.
Runtime edits use full Bendvy entity handles, including namespace and generation.
An absent parent detaches the object. Reparenting preserves the local transform.
It may change the object's world position. There is no preserve-world operation.
Runtime spawn and despawn remain outside this API.

Local transforms use column vectors and `T * R * S`. A root's GlobalTransform is
its local model matrix. A child's matrix is `parent_global * child_local`.
GlobalTransform retains the complete affine matrix, including shear. It is never
decomposed back into rotation and scale. World bounds enclose the eight transformed
corners of the source mesh AABB over all source vertices, including unused ones.
They bound that object's geometry, not its subtree. A mesh without vertices has
empty bounds. Lighting uses the inverse transpose of the
world linear transform. A singular transform is allowed for unlit geometry;
textured geometry requires a finite, numerically usable inverse: absolute
determinant at least `1e-30`, finite inverse entries, and inverse-column squared
lengths in `[1e-24,1e24]`. These are numerical admission limits, not a condition
number guarantee. Non-finite transformed corners reject the candidate. Quaternion
squared lengths retain the Creation tolerance `[0.9999,1.0001]`.
Textured roots also retain the flat renderer's local scale-magnitude limits
`[1e-6,1e6]`. Detachment validates those limits before publication.

Source bounds and the material's lighting requirement come from compilation.
They describe that scene's source geometry. Renderer-only geometry replacement
does not rebind ECS source metadata: recreate the scene from matching compiled
sources when changing its meshes or materials. Runtime mesh/material rebinding
and using these bounds for culling are outside this API.

Creation descriptions are immutable inputs. The ECS owns local transforms,
parent relationships, source bounds, and derived state. A completed tick or
accepted public edit publishes a consistent set of local transforms, globals,
and bounds. GlobalTransform and world bounds have no public setter. Detached
observations and render lists cannot write back to the world. A last-accepted
local value retained with derived state is a rollback checkpoint, not a second
simulation authority.

The baseline recomputes the complete forest sequentially at each publication
boundary. Validation and derivation finish before public edits write components.
A rejected public edit preserves the complete world. If a scheduled transform
update makes derivation invalid, local transforms return to their last accepted
values and existing derived values remain valid. Schedule administrative progress
is retained. The persistent RenderScene and incremental invalidation belong to E5.

## Description and runtime API sketch

`Creation.parent(instance, Some{index})` assigns a parent in a scene description.
`None{}` makes a root. Existing `Instance{mesh,material,transform}` remains a root.
Compilation validates relationships and derived numerical state before bootstrap.

`Scene.set_parent(app, entity, parent)` and `Scene.set_transform(app, entity, local)`
return the owned application beside an acceptance result. Invalid or stale
handles, invalid transforms, and invalid derived state return a diagnostic.
The same operations are available for the mesh application.

Version 1 JSON retains existing flat scenes. An optional `parent` is a zero-based
placement index or null. The placement transform is applied once at its first
part, which serves as the parent anchor; remaining parts attach to the anchor
with identity local transforms. This expansion is used only for scenes
with parent links, so old flat instance order and transform behavior remain intact.
Parent references address placements before model expansion. Empty models are
rejected in scenes containing parent links. Unknown fields and invalid references
remain errors.

Inheritance affects spatial state, not which entities a system chooses to move.
The existing demonstration's scheduled motion still edits every local transform.
To move an entire placement rigidly, edit its anchor; a system that separately
edits descendant locals adds their own motion to the inherited parent motion.

## Acceptance and required evidence

The production path is description → Creation/JSON validation → ECS columns →
sequential derivation → detached draws → shared offscreen/window draw recording.
The hierarchy evaluator, ECS publication adapter, normal payload, and renderer
preflight enforce the contract.

Required evidence includes:

- Formal claims in `LAWS.bend` against production definitions for composition,
  rejection, publication, and bounds derivation. Numerical properties additionally
  run in native Bend with explicit tolerance and independently calculated geometry.
- Actual ECS executions covering deep chains, branches, forward references,
  movement, rotation, nonuniform scale/shear, reparenting, detachment, independent
  branches, and exact preservation after invalid edits.
- Real Vulkan RGBA/D32 readbacks against an independently transformed mesh,
  including surface-normal lighting. Owned X11 execution and deterministic replay
  compare complete local/global/bounds state, not just a digest.
- Existing flat-scene, JSON, textured rendering, mesh, and window consumers.
- Passing baseline → deliberate production regression rejected at the named
  property → restored passing baseline. A build failure is not detection evidence.
- A source-specific `verify-workflow` receipt with every required stage complete.

## Performance evaluation plan

Measure sequential publication cost and its share of real rendering workloads
for flat, deep, and branching scenes. Count accepted updates and validate final
state/output. Use five interleaved runs per comparison and report median/range.
Inspect the machine load and use a separate profiling run to identify the limiter.
Consider improvement only if propagation exceeds 2 ms per 1000-node update or
adds over 10% to a representative frame. Set a concrete target before trying a
change. Allow at most three single-change attempts, retain only repeatable gains
with identical state/render output, and validate a winner on additional scenes.
Otherwise retain the straightforward implementation. No parallelism is planned.

# Public creation reference

`src/creation.bend` defines immutable scenes, instances, cameras, and compiled
ranges. Mesh and material source values come from
[`src/content.bend`](content.md). Constructors create ordinary unchecked values.
`compile(Scene)` is the checked entry point and returns
`Result<Error,Compiled>`. It needs neither Vulkan nor a window.

## Descriptions

- `Content.Vertex`, `Content.Mesh`, and `Content.Basic` follow the
  [mesh and material contract](content.md). RGB is finite but unrestricted in
  magnitude. Tint is finite and bounded to `[0,1]`.
- `Instance{mesh,material,transform}` creates one initial ECS entity.
  Translation and scale must be finite. Quaternion squared length must lie in
  `[0.9999,1.0001]`.
- `Parented{mesh,material,transform,parent}` attaches it to a zero-based source
  instance index. `Creation.parent(instance, Some{index})` sets that relationship;
  `None{}` detaches it. Forward references are allowed. See
  [scene hierarchy](scene-hierarchy.md) for composition and transactional edits.
- `Scene{instances}` preserves instance order through compilation and bootstrap.

`compile` first rejects more than 100,000 instances with `TooLarge`. It then
validates instances in source order. Each instance reports `BadMesh` before
`BadMaterial`, then `BadTransform`, carrying the zero-based instance position.
A source mesh over the current 381,300-vertex or 3,000,000-index profile reports
`BadMesh`. A new pair that overflows aggregate packed counts reports `TooLarge`.
A duplicate pair reuses its range before any aggregate growth check. Validation
and packing complete before any GPU allocation. Hierarchy derivation then rejects
missing parents, cycles, and invalid world transforms or bounds with `BadHierarchy`.

Compilation materializes only used mesh/material pairs. Bitwise structural
comparison identifies identical source values. First occurrences determine
range order. Repeated pairs share a range while retaining separate ECS entities.
References start at 7 to preserve the existing demonstration's mesh reference.
Applications consume generated references instead of selecting them.

`Compiled{seeds,geometry}` is the single result. Each `Seed{transform,mesh,spatial}`
contains the existing `MeshRef`, which identifies baked geometry. It is not an
entity identity. `spatial` contains the validated local relationship/source bounds,
global matrix, and world bounds. `Geometry{vertices,indices,ranges}` contains tinted vertices,
rebased indices, and `Range{id,first_index,index_count,texture}` values.
The texture is `None` for Basic materials and `Some{SourceImage}` for textured materials.
Positions, UVs, and normals remain unchanged. `resolve(ranges,id)` returns the matching range or `None`.

`Scene.create(seeds)` registers the existing Bendvy application. The first tick
queues and publishes initial entities, then runs the existing movement system.
Bendvy handles identify entities. Completed ticks derive globals and bounds before
observation. `Scene.set_transform` and `Scene.set_parent` consume and return the
application beside a `Result<Hierarchy.Error,Unit>`; rejected edits preserve it.
`Observe.spatial` returns detached entity/local/global/bounds rows. A second tick moves existing entities without
spawning them again. Reservation refusal retains ownership through the existing
bootstrap error path. There is no new runtime asset service or material column.

Both renderers accept `Geometry`, validate its bounds before allocating, and
preflight every extracted drawing before recording commands. They issue the
range's actual first index and count in extraction order with the existing
camera/model matrix push. Zero-index ranges issue no draw or push commands.
Geometry with no indices owns no vertex or index buffers. Framebuffer clears
and presentation still run.

## Camera

`Camera{target,yaw,pitch,distance,projection}` defines an orbit around `target`.
`Perspective{scale,near,far}` uses the vertical projection scale, equivalent to
`cot(vertical_fov / 2)`. All values must be finite. Distance, scale, and near
must be positive, and far must exceed near.

`camera(value)` returns `Some` for a valid configuration and `None` otherwise.
`view(camera,width,height)` returns a finite matrix or `None`. Invalid cameras,
zero dimensions, and non-finite derived matrices return `None`.
`default_camera()` preserves the old orbit and projection arithmetic. The demo
applies its own tick-one framing separately.

`Input.key` changes orbit values while preserving target and projection. Reset
restores yaw `0.65`, pitch `0.45`, and distance `7.0`, preserving the configured
target and lens. Reset does not restore a caller's custom initial orbit.
Controls retain the existing pitch clamp `[0.1,1.4]` and distance clamp `[4,15]`.

ranges. Mesh and material source values come from
[`src/content.bend`](content.md). Constructors create ordinary unchecked values.
`compile(Scene)` is the checked entry point and returns
`Result<Error,Compiled>`. It needs neither Vulkan nor a window.

## Descriptions

- `Content.Vertex`, `Content.Mesh`, and `Content.Basic` follow the
  [mesh and material contract](content.md). RGB is finite but unrestricted in
  magnitude. Tint is finite and bounded to `[0,1]`.
- `Instance{mesh,material,transform}` creates one initial ECS entity.
  Translation and scale must be finite. Quaternion squared length must lie in
  `[0.9999,1.0001]`.
- `Parented{mesh,material,transform,parent}` attaches it to a zero-based source
  instance index. `Creation.parent(instance, Some{index})` sets that relationship;
  `None{}` detaches it. Forward references are allowed. See
  [scene hierarchy](scene-hierarchy.md) for composition and transactional edits.
- `Scene{instances}` preserves instance order through compilation and bootstrap.

`compile` first rejects more than 100,000 instances with `TooLarge`. It then
validates instances in source order. Each instance reports `BadMesh` before
`BadMaterial`, then `BadTransform`, carrying the zero-based instance position.
A source mesh over the current 381,300-vertex or 3,000,000-index profile reports
`BadMesh`. A new pair that overflows aggregate packed counts reports `TooLarge`.
A duplicate pair reuses its range before any aggregate growth check. Validation
and packing complete before any GPU allocation. Hierarchy derivation then rejects
missing parents, cycles, and invalid world transforms or bounds with `BadHierarchy`.

Compilation materializes only used mesh/material pairs. Bitwise structural
comparison identifies identical source values. First occurrences determine
range order. Repeated pairs share a range while retaining separate ECS entities.
References start at 7 to preserve the existing demonstration's mesh reference.
Applications consume generated references instead of selecting them.

`Compiled{seeds,geometry}` is the single result. Each `Seed{transform,mesh,spatial}`
contains the existing `MeshRef`, which identifies baked geometry. It is not an
entity identity. `spatial` contains the validated local relationship/source bounds,
global matrix, and world bounds. `Geometry{vertices,indices,ranges}` contains tinted vertices,
rebased indices, and `Range{id,first_index,index_count,texture}` values.
The texture is `None` for Basic materials and `Some{SourceImage}` for textured materials.
Positions, UVs, and normals remain unchanged. `resolve(ranges,id)` returns the matching range or `None`.

`Scene.create(seeds)` registers the existing Bendvy application. The first tick
queues and publishes initial entities, then runs the existing movement system.
Bendvy handles identify entities. Completed ticks derive globals and bounds before
observation. `Scene.set_transform` and `Scene.set_parent` consume and return the
application beside a `Result<Hierarchy.Error,Unit>`; rejected edits preserve it.
`Observe.spatial` returns detached entity/local/global/bounds rows. A second tick moves existing entities without
spawning them again. Reservation refusal retains ownership through the existing
bootstrap error path. There is no new runtime asset service or material column.

Both renderers accept `Geometry`, validate its bounds before allocating, and
preflight every extracted drawing before recording commands. They issue the
range's actual first index and count in extraction order with the existing
camera/model matrix push. Zero-index ranges issue no draw or push commands.
Geometry with no indices owns no vertex or index buffers. Framebuffer clears
and presentation still run.

## Camera

`Camera{target,yaw,pitch,distance,projection}` defines an orbit around `target`.
`Perspective{scale,near,far}` uses the vertical projection scale, equivalent to
`cot(vertical_fov / 2)`. All values must be finite. Distance, scale, and near
must be positive, and far must exceed near.

`camera(value)` returns `Some` for a valid configuration and `None` otherwise.
`view(camera,width,height)` returns a finite matrix or `None`. Invalid cameras,
zero dimensions, and non-finite derived matrices return `None`.
`default_camera()` preserves the old orbit and projection arithmetic. The demo
applies its own tick-one framing separately.

`Input.key` changes orbit values while preserving target and projection. Reset
restores yaw `0.65`, pitch `0.45`, and distance `7.0`, preserving the configured
target and lens. Reset does not restore a caller's custom initial orbit.
Controls retain the existing pitch clamp `[0.1,1.4]` and distance clamp `[4,15]`.

# Game Engine in Bend — Roadmap

**Revision:** 6 · November 5, 2026 · updated for E4 scene hierarchy

**Engine repository:** [Entangle on Entire](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/entangle). **Vulkan library:** [bend-vulkan on Entire](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/bend-vulkan).

**Status:** E0, E1, and E2 are complete on `main` through `2faa879` [S24–S37]. Entangle has two interactive non-voxel applications: the moving 100-entity scene and the mesh playground with a controllable object. App extraction, static startup registration, public scene creation, bounded fixed steps, the sequential step contract, and CPU-only headless execution are implemented and verified within the limits below. E3 is complete on `main` under the documented trust limits [S52]. The selected upload-range checker [S38] has a [kernel-checked universal containment proof](docs/upload-range.md). Both production renderers enforce that exact checker through a shared buffer API, with repository verification rejecting ordinary API bypasses [S39]. Scoped native ABI and exact transport-limit verification pass [S40]. Both renderers support [mesh replacement with deferred destruction](docs/mesh-replacement.md) [S48]. Retention verification covers recorded and unsubmitted commands, multiple submissions, uniform and sampled-image descriptor slots and sets, and memory aliases [S49, S52]. Native failure handling is verified through real-runtime checks and bounded proofs of production handlers [S50, S51]. E4 has landed the [Asset API](docs/assets.md), [internal source format](docs/content.md), and [PNG decoder](docs/image-decoder.md) on `main` through `90c7b7e`. The bounded [OBJ importer](docs/model-obj.md) is verified and merged on `main` through `a016c6b`. The [S44 JSON loader](docs/json-scene.md) is on `main` at `ac805c7`; [textured rendering](docs/textured-materials.md) is on `main` at `dc70d54` [S53]. [Scene hierarchy](docs/scene-hierarchy.md) is implemented locally; its final source-specific verification is in progress under [Trail 31](https://entire.com/et/bend-engine/-/trails/31) [S54]. The remaining E4 tasks, E5–E7, and R0–R4 are planned. `v0.1-alpha` remains an E5 milestone.

**Goal:** an independent, modular game engine, with Bevy-like modularity but a simulation core designed around Bend's computational model. Engine logic and new algorithms are implemented in Bend; native code stays at the system boundary.

**Next release:** `v0.1-alpha` — two non-voxel applications, a public API, a persistent scene representation, and the first practically useful proven guarantee.

**Initial platform:** Linux x86-64, using the existing X11/Vulkan path.

**Schedule:** no calendar deadlines; each stage ends with a verifiable result.

**Dependency research:** the Jonlib and BendHub review supplies candidates for E4 and R0–R2 [S41–S47]. Subsequent runtime qualification selected Jonlib's narrow PNG and OBJ modules behind engine APIs. The [OBJ evidence](docs/verification/2026-11-04-model-obj/README.md) records its supported profile and validation limits. The completed [S41 math evaluation](docs/verification/2026-11-05-jonmath/README.md) retains Entangle's production math after explicit adapter qualification and exact retained-scene comparisons. E4 remains incomplete.

## E1 progress, November 3, 2026

- Completed the separate engine project and native dependency-pinning task in Entangle. Exact commits and compiler requirements are in [toolchain.bend](toolchain.bend); Git submodules retain the dependency revisions.
- `bend tools/verify.bend` passed on Linux x86-64. One native executable runs the upstream scheduled-health consumer and Vulkan buffer roundtrip. The check compares the complete ECS output and requires zero live Vulkan objects after cleanup [S25].
- Project component records, exact defaults, structural laws, and a native field-preservation consumer are implemented.
- The registered scene creates 100 entities once and translates each by `(1.0, 0.5, -2.0)` per tick. An explicit publication barrier makes the new entities visible before movement on tick 1. All entities retain logical mesh ID 7, rotation, scale, and full entity identities across eight native ticks [S26].
- `Observe.draw_list` extracts only complete transforms and mesh references. It returns the retained application separately and shares the observer's ordered component traversal. Proofs and native checks passed for empty extraction, repeated extraction, retained lists across ticks, and inspector and world-clock preservation [S27].
- The offscreen renderer consumes the actual detached `DrawList`, uploads one shared mesh per scope, and reuses Vulkan resources. Bend computes complete translation, quaternion rotation, scale, and camera transforms. No new C code or dependency changes were needed [S28].
- The full verifier passed with clean dependency checkouts and unchanged pins. It includes the dependency baseline, component consumer, shared-mesh scene, and offscreen renderer. The final reviewed native build also passed Khronos synchronization validation on the GTX 1660, with zero live objects after cleanup. Entangle window checks, sanitizers, benchmarks, and the full upstream suites were not part of this run [S28].

- Entangle now renders the actual shared-mesh DrawList in the existing native window path. The separate window driver verified live ECS movement, retained tick-one camera replay, repeated resizing, hidden polling and ticks, Escape, hidden Close, input rejection, and terminal cleanup on the GTX 1660 with Khronos synchronization validation [S29].

- Reviewed CPU/GPU baseline timings and counters complete the final E1 task [S30]. The window runs satisfy E1's moving-scene, controllable-camera, resize, and exit criteria. The App extraction reran these checks without changing their results [S31]. E1 is complete.

## E2 progress, November 3, 2026

- Extracted shared App resource scope, time policy, camera input, event draining, and Action error handling. Concrete scene state and verification live in `examples/scene-window-app.bend`.
